articles.title: Cincinnati Bengals: Could Joe Burrow's injury trigger a move for Kirk Cousins, asks Neil Reynolds?
articles.summary: Get the thoughts of Sky Sports NFL presenter Neil Reynolds in his weekly column 'The Final Word'; he reflects on a stirring win for the Detroit Lions, the pressure increasing on the Miami Dolphins, and ponders what the Cincinnati Bengals should do to cover the injured Joe Burrow at QB
articles.body:
It was really impressive to see how the Detroit Lions bounced back from that Week One defeat to the Green Bay Packers.

They were very motivated to show that they can exist without former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who was on the other sideline leading the Chicago Bears.

This was a huge game for head coach Dan Campbell, new OC John Morton and for Jared Goff, who was excellent, and a scoreline of 52-21 was emphatic.

I didn't expect the New York Giants' visit to the Dallas Cowboys to become a modern-day classic, but it felt like that as they went back and forth.

Russell Wilson was excellent for most of the game, and Dak Prescott was bold and attacking.

The two teams went toe to toe; Prescott thought he'd won it with a touchdown pass to George Pickens with 52 seconds left, only for Wilson to think he'd won it with a touchdown pass to Malik Nabers with 25 seconds left.

Brandon Aubrey then kicked things into overtime, where he'd finish the job on a huge, needed win for the Cowboys. For the Giants, this game was at least a big boost after having not scored an offensive touchdown in Week One.

The Indianapolis Colts had a dramatic win over the Denver Broncos with a twice-taken field goal from Spencer Shrader.

But the story for me is Daniel Jones, who threw for over 300 yards and a touchdown pass. It's his second-straight week with a good performance as the new quarterback for the Colts.

As for Indianapolis, they're the first team in the Super Bowl era not to punt in their first two games - incredible!

Jones maybe doesn't have the high ceiling like backup QB Anthony Richardson, but I think head coach Shane Steichen wants someone he can rely on and someone he can coach from down to down - and it is paying dividends early in the season for the Colts.

Eagles beat Chiefs in Super Bowl rematch

The Philadelphia Eagles won the Super Bowl 59 rematch against the Kansas City Chiefs.

For me, this match was all about their physicality, their depth and their strength. It wasn't flashy, there weren't too many big plays - especially through the air - from Jalen Hurts, other than one long throw to DeVonta Smith.

The Eagles are built on power and the strength of their roster. It's a complete team effort.

On the other side, Patrick Mahomes is 0-2 for the first time in his NFL career, also losing three games in a row for the first time since entering the league.

It's not his fault. Mahomes fights for every yard on the field, puts his body on the line in the process but he just doesn't get enough help. The Chiefs have turned him into an expensive game manager.

The pressure is really building on the Miami Dolphins after their 33-27 loss to the New England Patriots.

It looks like head coach Mike McDaniel is aging before our very eyes. The stress is really showing on him, with Tyreek Hill frustrated too as Tua Tagovailoa fails to get the job done - the quarterback then biting back at his receiver in the media.

Miami go on the road to the Buffalo Bills in Week Three, meaning they could leave with an 0-3 record that would only put more pressure on McDaniel. His seat is getting hotter by the minute.

Player of the Week - Jared Goff, QB, Detroit Lions

There's a lot been said about Goff, about how he's been helped out over the years by the likes of offensive coaches Sean McVay and Ben Johnson.

Sunday against Detroit was a chance for him to show that's he's absolutely fine standing on his own two feet or working with a new coordinator.

He had over 300 yards passing, five touchdowns and zero interceptions - pretty much perfection.

Coach of the Week - Dan Campbell, Detroit Lions

I'm picking Campbell, for much the same reasons as Goff.

He had a lot to prove and had to settle down his team, with a bit of panic evident in the Lions during the first week of the season.

He has instilled some confidence in them and showed them the way forward. They are loaded with talent, they're going to be good still, they just had a bad week at the office in Week One.

Campbell sent all the right messages to his team and it paid off on Sunday.

Play of the Week - Brandon Aubrey's field goal

I'm not going to go with a touchdown run, nor a touchdown pass. What about instead, Aubrey's game-tying field goal for the Cowboys as time expired in Dallas?

With barely a sweep of his leg, it went 64 yards for the game-tying field goal to sent things to overtime.

It was so nonchalant, so effortless, that when he lined up for a 46-yarder on the final play of overtime, it felt like it was going to be an easy chip shot - he made it and Dallas got their first win.

On the radar... Joe Burrow and QB injuries

What do the Cincinnati Bengals do moving forward? It's a hammer blow to lose Joe Burrow for three months to a toe injury.

There is no replacing a man who led the NFL in passing yards and passing touchdowns last season, but do they swing a trade for backups Kirk Cousins (Atanta Falcons) or Jameis Winston (Giants)?

Those teams will smell the desperation and pump up the price, so the Bengals probably stick with Jake Browning and hang on for dear life.

Whoever it will be, they won't be Burrow, so the Bengals are in a lot of trouble right now, even though they're 2-0.

He is one of a number of quarterback injuries to monitor leading into Week Three: JJ McCarthy is out for the Minnesota Vikings, meaning it's Carson Wentz's time, and will it still be Mac Jones for the San Francisco 49ers instead of Brock Purdy?

Also, keep an eye on Washington Commanders star QB Jayden Daniels with a knee injury... will they have to turn to backup Marcus Mariota?

Some early worries at the game's most important position.

articles.title: NFL: Cleveland Browns star Myles Garrett traded to Los Angeles Rams as Odell Beckham Jr. makes sensational New York Giants return
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have agreed terms on a trade to send defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown is traded to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick; Odell Beckham re-signs with the New York Giants
articles.body:
The trade is pending Garrett's physical examination and sees the Browns receive a 2027 first-round pick and pass rusher Jared Verse in return.

Garrett - who broke the NFL record for single season sacks with 23 in his last campiagn - with had previously issued a trade request but ended speculation when he signed a four-year, $160m (£118m) extension in 2025 with more than $122m (£90m) guaranteed.

However, the Browns finished the season 5-12 and plummeted to their second successive NFC north fourth-place finish, meaning that the franchise has missed the playoffs in seven of Garrett's nine seasons.

The defensive end reignited trade speculation when he missed the Browns' voluntary off-season training programme, and did not meet with new head coach Todd Monken after he replaced Kevin Stefanski earlier this year.

The Browns agreed to a restructured contract with Garrett that deferred $29m (£21m) dollars in bonus payments to September, giving Cleveland salary cap space to trade the pass-rusher - though they will still suffer a combined $40m (£29m) hit from Garrett's contract in the next two years.

The trade ends a lengthy nine-year tenure for Garrett since his selection by the Browns as the No 1 draft pick in 2017. He will join a Rams side that were one game away from the Super Bowl last season, and boast one Super Bowl title and a staggering 10 playoff wins under head coach Sean McVey.

The Los Angeles side will no doubt be buoyed by the addition of the best defensive player in the NFL.

A.J. Brown traded to the Patriots to end Eagles off-field turmoil

Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown has been traded to the New England Patriots for a 2028 first-round and a 2027 fifth-round pick, ending an illustrious but troubled tenure with the Super Bowl LIX champions.

Brown finishes his tenure with the Eagles with over 5000 receiving yards and a Super Bowl ring having made history as the only Eagles player ever to eclipse 1000 receiving yards in four consecutive seasons, though leaves under a cloud of controversy after numerous off-field issues marred his last two campiagns with the Eagles.

Brown was heavily criticised for telling fans on a twitch stream that they should "get rid" of him from their NFL fantasy teams - highlighting his dissatisfaction with his role on the team - before Eagles security guard Dom DiSandro had to physically separate the wide receiver and his head coach Nick Sirianni in a heated spat during the team's playoff loss to the 49ers in January.

Eagles GM Howie Roseman trading up to select highly-touted wide receiver Makai Lemon in the first round of this year's draft all but sealed Brown's fate - but they saved $7m (£5.2m) in cap space by waiting until June 1 to make the trade

The Patriots, though, secure another weapon for young quarterback Drake Maye as they look to eclipse their loss in the AFC Championship and go one better to the Super Bowl this campaign.

Odell Beckham Jr. makes sensational NFL return to former team Giants

Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has been signed by his former team, the New York Giants - in a remarkable move that secures the former pro-bowler a long-awaited return to the NFL after a season's absence.

Beckham made his name with the Giants after being selected 12th in the 2014 draft, then acheiving three consecutive 1300+ yard seasons to cement his name as one of the premier wide receivers in the league.

The American is also famous for recording one of the NFL's most iconic moments in a Giants jersey, when he recorded a 43-yard touchdown reception against the Dallas Cowboys that is widely regarded as the greatest catch in NFL history.

His recent NFL history, though, has been marred with controversy. Beckham was suspended for six games in 2025 for violating the league's performance-enhancing drugs policy, and remained unsigned throughout the season - he only managed nine catches for 55 yards in nine games for the Miami Dolphins during the previous campaign.

The wide receiver, though, appears to have got his happy ending in returning to the team that drafted him, joining forces once again with head coach John Harbaugh, who coached Beckham to 35 catches and 565 yards with the Baltimore Ravens in the 2023 season.

articles.title: Russell Wilson announces NFL retirement as former Seattle Seahawks quarterback takes up TV role
articles.summary: Russell Wilson led the Seattle Seahawks to their first Super Bowl win back in the 2013 season; he threw for 46,966 yards, with 353 touchdown passes and 114 interceptions across an NFL career spanning 14 years
articles.body:
"As I enter this next chapter with CBS Sports and 'The NFL Today,' I'm so blessed to continue doing what I love most - being around the greatest game in the world," he said in a video posted on his social media accounts.

Wilson played 14 seasons after being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft out of NC State. He spent his first 10 seasons with the Seahawks, leading them to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.

He was traded to Denver after the 2021 season and spent two rocky years with the Broncos before playing one season in Pittsburgh and another for the New York Giants.

Wilson threw for 46,966 yards, with 353 touchdown passes and 114 interceptions.

He joins Peyton Manning and Dan Marino as the only quarterbacks to throw at least 20 touchdown passes in each of their first three seasons and is one of seven quarterbacks to be selected to 10 Pro Bowls.

Wilson is the only player in NFL history with at least 30 touchdown passes and fewer than 15 interceptions in four straight seasons. He also had three seasons with at least 30 TD passes and 500 yards rushing, which is the most in NFL history.

In the video he thanked his teammates, friends and family and gave special thanks to former Seahawks coach Pete Carroll.

"Thanks for taking a chance on a young, 5-11 Black kid from Richmond, Virginia, that was told he was too small to ever make it in the NFL," Wilson said.

Wilson is the shortest starting quarterback to win a Super Bowl.

Wilson will replace Matt Ryan, who joined the Atlanta Falcons as president of football after two seasons on "The NFL Today." Wilson had considered returning for a 15th season, telling the New York Post last month that he was mulling an offer to join the New York Jets and back up Geno Smith.

His video featured highlights from his career and footage of him visiting patients at Seattle Children's Hospital. It ended with him thanking his wife, Ciara, and the sport he dedicated his life to.

"I thank you, football. ... I am forever grateful," he said.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback to make over $500m guaranteed after signing contract extension
articles.summary: Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has signed a contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs for two years; the deal is the NFL's first fully guaranteed $500m contract and keeps Mahomes' contract as the biggest in sports history
articles.body:
Mahomes, a three-time Super Bowl winner, will extend his contract by two years through to 2033 in a deal worth $504.75m.

The entire sum will be guaranteed through contract clauses and 30-year-old Mahomes can earn up to $522.25m through incentives - after signing the initial $477m-guaranteed deal in 2020.

The extension begins in 2027 and is worth $64 million a year, making it the highest yearly average salary in the NFL and the biggest contract in sports history.

Mahomes boasts a 95-31 career record and is 17-4 in the playoffs, while averaging the highest passing yards in NFL history at 285.2 per game and winning two NFL MVPs along the way.

The Chiefs, though, had their first losing season with Mahomes at the helm in 2025, as the team were 6-8 before Mahomes suffered an ACL injury in December and missed the last three games of the season (all losses).

The contract extension is a vote of confidence in the most successful player in their franchise's history.

"What's up Chiefs Kingdom, I'm just so excited to be here for life," Mahomes said.

"And to be part of the Chiefs Kingdom for even longer. We have so much more to do, let's go out and do it. Let's go and win some more."

Mahomes is now paid over $170m more guaranteed money than his closest competitor - the $330m contract of Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen - as he looks to cement his legacy and take his side to a third Super Bowl victory in eight seasons as a starter.

Chiefs general manager Brett Veach said: "This is a huge day for the Chiefs, Patrick, and really all of Chiefs Kingdom.

"This is a landmark deal for a once-in-a-lifetime player. Patrick has grown into one of the most prolific quarterbacks to ever play the game, and to add to that, he's changed the culture of our building and has led us in the most successful era in our franchise's history.

"Beyond the game, he's an incredible person who puts his team and winning above everything else.

"For Patrick, we know he's more motivated than ever to get back out there and lead us. I'm happy for him and his family, and excited for our future together."

articles.title: NFL: Detroit Lions player Terrion Arnold charged with leading plot to kidnap and pistol-whip three people
articles.summary: Terrion Arnold, who turned himself in on Wednesday, briefly appeared in court by video as a judge announced the charges; 23-year-old had 31 tackles and an interception last season for the Detroit Lions; he was a first-round pick in the 2024 draft after playing at the University of Alabama
articles.body:
Arnold, 23, who has also been charged with armed robbery, could face up to life in prison if found guilty.

Three men in their late teens were held at gunpoint, struck and robbed at an apartment in Tampa, Florida on February 4 of this year, said police, who claim Arnold was the "primary conspirator".

That incident occurred three days after possessions worth over $250,000 (approx £189,400) were reportedly stolen from Arnold and others at a rental property in Largo, around 20 miles west of Tanpa.

Investigators said the victims had nothing to do with the theft.

Arnold, who turned himself in on Wednesday, briefly appeared in court by video as a judge announced the charges.

He will remain in jail until at least a detention hearing on Monday.

At least seven people reportedly face charges.

The victims told police that Arnold's friends lured them to an apartment, held them at gunpoint and hit them while streaming the attack to Arnold.

Denise White, the CEO of the EAG Sports Management agency that represents Arnold, said there is "no credible evidence" against the player.

White added: "The government appears to be relying on testimony from multiple convicted felons who have admitted their own involvement and may have substantial incentives to shift blame in an effort to lessen their sentences.

"Mr Arnold looks forward to his day in court and is confident that the judicial process will lead to his ultimate vindication."

Arnold, a first-round pick in the 2024 draft after playing at the University of Alabama, had 31 tackles and an interception last season for the Lions.

The Lions and the NFL said they were aware of Arnold's arrest but declined to comment.

articles.title: Chris Johnson: Former Tennessee Titans running back reveals MND/ALS diagnosis
articles.summary: Former running back Chris Johnson enjoyed a glittering career in the NFL, making 130 appearances for the Tennessee Titans, New York Jets and Arizona Cardinals before retiring in 2018
articles.body:
The 40-year-old, a former NFL offensive player of the year who last played in 2017, said on ABC's Good Morning America that he had been diagnosed with the disease last year.

"We hoped it was something else, but after thorough testing, they finally came down with a diagnosis of ALS," said Johnson in an interview with Michael Strahan in which he had to use a voice modulator because the disease has already taken away his ability to speak.

ALS - the most common type of Motor Neurone Disease and the term most often used in the USA along with Lou Gehrig's disease - is a nervous system disease that affects nerve cells that control muscles throughout the body.

The disease leads to muscle weakness and other symptoms that get progressively worse.

Johnson said he was sharing his diagnosis because if it helps "even one person" get diagnosed sooner or gives another family hope "then it's worth it".

"It's continued to progress much faster than I ever imagined," Johnson said.

"I want people to understand just how quickly ALS can attack your body.

"Just over a year ago, I was picking up my seven-year-old daughter so she'd make a wish with her birthday cake. Today, I couldn't do that."

Johnson added: "I want people to know that I'm still me. ALS has changed what my body can do, but it hasn't changed who I am.

"People sometimes look at the physical disability and assume you're not still the same person inside. I still think the same. I still dream. I still love my family. My body just doesn't cooperate."

Johnson said in the interview that he was diagnosed with the illness last year, aged 39.

He added that there was no history of the disease in his family, adding: "My doctors believe my case is what's called sporadic ALS, which is actually how the vast majority of ALS cases happen.

"That is one of the reasons why this disease can be so shocking. It can happen to someone who never expected it."

Johnson, who was born in Orlando, Florida, attended East Carolina University. He was later snapped up by the Tennessee Titans in the 2008 AFL draft as a first-round, 24th overall pick.

The three-time Pro Bowler led the league for rushing yards (2,006) the following season - earning him the nickname CJ2K - and would go on to make a whopping 9,651 yards across his career, scoring 55 touchdowns in the process.

After spending five years at the Titans, he joined up with the New York Jets for a season in 2014 before moving to the Arizona Cardinals the following year. Johnson would make 130 NFL appearances during his career, starting in 111 of those games.

Johnson would first retire from the NFL after 10 years in the game in November 2018, before signing a one-day contract to retire as a Tennessee Titan in April 2019.

articles.title: NFL: Detroit Lions release Terrion Arnold after judge sets bail at $1m as cornerback charged with leading plot to kidnap three people
articles.summary: Terrion Arnold's bail was set at $1m as the cornerback faces eight felony charges for allegedly orchestrating a plot to kidnap three people at gunpoint; 23-year-old was drafted to the Lions in 2024 and has made 24 appearances
articles.body:
The Lions announced the news on X on Monday, after a Florida judge set the 23-year-old's bail at $1m (£750,000).

Prosecutors said three people in their late teens were held at gunpoint, beaten and robbed at an apartment in Tampa, Florida on February 4. One of the victims was a driver who worked for Arnold, and at least seven people are facing charges.

The alleged incident took place three days after Arnold had over $250,000 (approx £189,400) worth of luxury possessions, including watches, cash and designer bags, stolen from himself and others at a property in Largo, 20 miles west of Tampa.

However, investigators found the victims were not involved in the robbery.

The victims said the cornerback's friends had coaxed them into a property in which they held them at gunpoint and beat them. They added the abduction was streamed to Arnold.

On Wednesday, Arnold turned himself in to police and had briefly appeared in court, where a judge read out the eight felony charges against him.

Chief Court Judge Christopher Sabella granted him bail and said he would not be required to wear an ankle monitor as it would hinder his ability to tackle during games and training.

His representative, Denise White, the CEO of EAG Sports Management, said the judges' ruling "confirms that there is very little evidence to even suggest any criminal involvement by Mr Arnold."

None of Arnold's co-defendants were granted bail. Two have pleaded guilty and are cooperating with authorities. Prosecutors say their statements tie Arnold, who was not at the apartment, to the crimes.

In addition, prosecutors argue Arnold is as responsible for the crimes as his co-defendants because he told his associates that he thought he knew who had stolen from him and said he wanted to confront them, setting events in motion.

Erin Maloney, a spokesperson for the state attorney's office, said: "Our office remains committed to seeking justice for the three victims in the case who were beaten, robbed, and held against their will."

The American footballer's legal counsel, Harvey Steinberg, told the court on Monday that prosecutors are "not even close" to showing Arnold that he knew or instructed his co-defendants.

Arnold was drafted to the Lions as a first-round 24th overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, having played his college football for the Alabama Crimson Tide.

During his two seasons in the NFL, Arnold made 24 appearances for the Lions (22 starts) and made 91 tackles while defending 18 passes.

articles.title: Myles Garrett, Patrick Mahomes and Jesse Minter: The NFL's biggest storylines on road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season gets under way this week as the Buffalo Bills face the Houston Texans from 6pm Sunday live on Sky Sports, followed by the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles and the Dallas Cowboys against the New York Giants in Sunday Night Football
articles.body:
The new campaign begins on Wednesday night when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks take on the New England Patriots, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am in the early hours of Thursday.

The phrase 'all in' can be over-exhausted at times in the NFL, but rarely has it been as glaringly-fitting than in the case of the 2026 Los Angeles Rams. They made the biggest move of the offseason by acquiring reigning Defensive Player of the Year and generational pass rusher Myles Garrett in a blockbuster trade with the Cleveland Browns, traded for Kansas City Chiefs star cornerback Trent McDuffie, reunited him with free agent corner Jaylen Watson and welcomed back Aaron Donald as the three-time Defensive Player of the Year came out of retirement to forge one of the most frightening defensive tandems in NFL history alongside Garrett.

Stop them and there is already an existing core of Byron Young, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske and chess piece safety Quentin Lake for which to account.

They enter the season led by reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback, have one of the league's most talented wide receivers in Puka Nacua, boast an upper-tier rushing attack of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum and just produced the NFL's most potent offense on the way to the NFC Championship Game last year, where they fell short against the champion Seattle Seahawks in a game more Super Bowl-esque than the Super Bowl itself. They are favourites for a reason.

The Baltimore Ravens are desperate to cash in on the prime of their generational quarterback, and so moved on from head coach John Harbaugh after 18 seasons this year in view of a fresh look to their Super Bowl charge. They would turn to former Los Angeles Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter and former Chicago Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle as the men to help Lamar Jackson lead the Ravens over the line following a playoff-less campaign on the back of three Divisional Round exits and an AFC Championship Game defeat in six seasons.

Between Jackson, Derrick Henry and Doyle's offensive scheme, the Ravens have the potential to be one of the league's most destructive play-action run-heavy attacks. Questions remain of a receiving core spearheaded by Zay Flowers, but there are high expectations for third-round rookie Ja'Kobi Lane.

A slow start and marquee injuries, namely to Jackson himself, cost Baltimore in 2025, so too one of the worst pass defenses in football. Minter had been instrumental in transforming the Chargers' defense during his time alongside Harbaugh, and arrives armed with the personnel to orchestrate one of the league's best units behind all-action safety Kyle Hamilton, a returning Nnamdi Madubuike and offseason addition Trey Hendrickson.

Despite his demise in Miami, former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel remains one of football's most prized offensive architects as he takes his expertise over to California. There he has been tasked with unlocking the best of Justin Herbert as the new offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Chargers, whose franchise quarterback is yet to shake the monkey of a first career playoff win off his back. For all the blockbuster arm talent, Herbert's chief criticism remains his modest postseason record, but McDaniel and his whacky wizardry is in town to change that.

It remains a team somewhat built on 'ifs' as far as their AFC West challenge is concerned. 'If' star offensive tackle tandem Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater can rediscover their best after combining for just six games due to injury last season, 'if' running back Omarion Hampton can be a difference-maker, 'if' Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston is enough firepower for Herbert on the outside, 'if' first-round pick Akheem Mesidor can make an immediate impact to a slightly understaffed pass rush, 'if' Tuli Tuipulotu, Derwin James and a 35-year-old Khalil Mack can preserve Minter's influence with last season's top-10 defense.

Herbert is a freak, but he is not immune to queries, and this is his best chance yet to firmly nestle himself among the AFC's perennial contenders.

It was a strange 2025 season in Philly, where the Eagles clinched the NFC East division title amid a storm of locker room tension and frequent offensive sputters during the defence of their Super Bowl title. It would culminate in a wild-card round defeat to the San Francisco 49ers and the eventual departure of wantaway wide receiver AJ Brown, who appeared to drift from quarterback Jalen Hurts while being critical of Kevin Patullo's play-calling within an attack that slumped to 24th in total yards.

Patullo was fired as offensive coordinator this offseason and replaced by former Green Bay Packers quarterback coach Sean Mannion, who will turn to DeVonta Smith as his No 1 passing threat along with a new supporting cast of Hollywood Brown, Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon in the Eagles' bid to adapt to life without Brown.

Legendary coach Jeff Stoutland retired this offseason, but leaves what remains one of the league's most accomplished offensive lines. Behind it sits Saquon Barkley, whose cut exploits should thrive in Mannion's outside zone plant-and-go scheme as he responds to a perceived 'down' year. On the opposite side of the ball Vic Fangio still pulls the strings to one of the most talent-rich personnel groups among NFL defenses, for which there appears zero concerns. All eyes turn to the Hurts and Mannion marriage.

The Kansas City Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season on the back of reaching seven straight AFC Championship games and five Super Bowls in six campaigns, three of which they won. It was also the first time since 2015 that they failed to win the AFC West, slumping to third with a record of 6-11 as offensive frailties finally caught up with them. To make matters worse quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending torn ACL and LCL in December, for which he underwent immediate surgery. He is back - but how back? And are THEY back?

Andy Reid's dynasty men had found themselves in a rare place on the periphery, Mahomes enduring his worst statistical campaign and a once high-powered attack finally fizzling out into nothingness having long-been rescued by Steve Spagnuolo's defense. You would be hard pushed arguing Mahomes is not still the NFL's best quarterback, and hard pushed believing he will not wrestle back his command of the league at some stage, but the Chiefs await to see just how quickly he can get back to being the same dynamic out-of-structure menace in the wake of his recovery.

Travis Kelce is not the same defining wrinkle to Reid's playbook at the age of 36, while Rashee Rice faces a 'prove it' year as Mahomes' lead receiver after playing just eight games in 2025. The Chiefs did, though, seek to ease their quarterback's return by signing Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III as a new dimension to an uninspiring backfield, while replacing Matt Nagy with returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, a popular figure in their past Super Bowl success. A Mahomes, Reid and Spagnuolo trio might, meanwhile, still be the best in football.

Sean Payton's Championship-contender Denver Broncos will not give up the AFC West easily, though.

Joe Burrow insists he is tired of waiting, tired of kicking Cincinnati's Super Bowl can down the road, tired of saying 'next time'; for him, this is it, the chance to get back to the 'Big Dance', the chance to win it all. Rarely do you doubt his confidence, rarely do you not believe in his ability to lift a Lombardi, but between injuries, including to Burrow himself, and roster imbalance the Bengals have never quite worked it out since falling at the final hurdle against the Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

They have now missed the playoffs in three straight seasons, an astonishing mini-drought considering that, behind Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can be one of the most explosive aerial attacks in football.

An apparent move towards more play-action and under-center looks is a fascinating and long-coveted wrinkle to a Bengals offense criticised for becoming stale at times under Zac Taylor. In truth, though, it has never really been deficiencies on offense to prompt their struggles, but instead their consistent issues on defense. They just traded a first-round pick for Dexter Lawrence and acquired edge rusher Boye Mafe - but is it enough?

'Run it forward' was the term used by Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald this offseason as Seattle prepare to defend their Super Bowl crown following February's dominant win over the New England Patriots. And there is no reason they cannot map out a route back to February's finale.

Kenneth Walker's exit raises some fresh uncertainty in the backfield, but this is still a complete roster brimming with playmakers and overseen by perhaps the top defensive mastermind in the league currently. Sam Darnold is coming off a season in which he performed like a top-10 quarterback to shun critics for good, feeding Jaxon Smith-Njigba on his way to a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards.

Macdonald and Aden Durde's defense, meanwhile, ranked first in EPA per drive and first in points allowed with little evidence of a decline threat. Besides Walker and the addition of rookie running back Jadarian Price, the one sizeable change comes on the sidelines as Brian Fleury takes over play-calling duties for the first time following offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak's departure to become head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Nonetheless, another Super Bowl run is on the cards.

It feels like a different story in New England, where you cannot help but brace for the possibility of regression for a Patriots team that flew ahead of schedule by reaching the Super Bowl. It would end in a humbling defeat to a far greater Seahawks team, but that should not deter from Drake Maye announcing himself as a long-term solution to the Patriots' quarterback problems. He reaped the rewards of daring to be the most aggressive passer in football, and the Patriots provided him with much-needed perimeter depth this offseason by welcoming AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs.

TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson are capable of joining the best rushing attacks in the league, Christian Gonzalez is an elite cornerstone on a defense that ranked eighth in yards and fourth in points, but there are still concerns in the trenches over a lack of star quality to their pass rush and an offensive line that allowed 47 sacks last year.

Nothing underlines the Mahomes and Reid effect quite like the sight of the Buffalo Bills firing Sean McDermott, the Baltimore Ravens parting with Harbaugh and Burrow's call for urgency to the Cincinnati Bengals' Super Bowl push. Granted, Mahomes and Reid did not dump any of them out last season, but it is for Kansas City's dynasty dominance that the agony of all three has been prolonged, particularly in the case of Josh Allen and the Bills.

Much like Jackson in Baltimore, the Bills have a responsibility to maximise the best of their alien quarterback, behind whom they have been banging on the Super Bowl door. They are nursing the wounds of fresh playoff disappointment after suffering an overtime loss to the Broncos to mark their fourth divisional-round defeat in the last five years, as much prompting the end of McDermott's reign. Joe Brady was subsequently promoted to head coach while Jim Leonhard was hired as Buffalo's new defensive coordinator in the organisation's bid to get over the line.

For as long as Allen is healthy and on the field, the Bills will remain Super Bowl contenders. There is a strong case for him being the league's most defining 'X factor' such has become his ability to strap an entire team to his back while combining for the most total touchdowns by any quarterback since entering the league in 2018. It is for him, with the help of last season's league rushing leader James Cook, that the Bills rarely stray from a place at the top of offensive rankings.

This year's marquee addition is wide receiver DJ Moore, while the major interest lies with a new-look defense that introduces Bradley Chubb and CJ Gardner-Johnson following something of an exodus including Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White.

Liam Coen and Ben Johnson both issued a warning of new contenders to the rest of the league during impressive maiden seasons as the respective head coaches of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears, each punching a ticket to the playoffs and each finding joy with their No 1-pick quarterbacks. Will they take the next step?

Trevor Lawrence delivered the most clinical, most commanding year of his Jags career by a distance as he threw for 4,007 yards and 29 touchdowns to 12 interceptions while also rushing for nine scores on the way to the wild-card round, where Coen's side were eventually stopped by the Buffalo Bills. It featured an eight-game winning streak to finish the campaign as the Jags' offense took flight alongside an Anthony Campanile that ranked fifth in EPA/play. Questions come in a backfield that just lost its chief rushing threat in Travis Etienne, making for a new-look committee attack led by Bhayshul Tuten.

Elsewhere, Johnson lived up to his billing as one of the most exciting modern offensive minds in football as he won 11 games in his first year while taking the Bears to the divisional-round of the playoffs. He conjured one of the most dynamic rushing schemes in the league and proved the perfect coach to put Caleb Williams in positions to succeed, cutting down on the negative plays and embracing his proclivity for the spectacular. Sure, accuracy inconsistencies are still under the microscope, but the makings of a formidable coach-quarterback tandem are there. Chicago's bigger concern is perhaps its shortage of pass rush threats.

Will the Cowboys and Texans make elite units count?

Only the Los Angeles Rams flaunted a more potent offense than the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 as a triple-threat of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens through the air was complemented by long-awaited rushing success thanks largely to Javonte Williams.

The stunning decision to trade away Micah Parsons was, meanwhile, followed by the Cowboys' defense ranking third-worst in yards allowed, worst against the pass, and worst in points allowed. It became a point of focus this offseason as the Cowboys hired Christian Parker as their new defensive coordinator, traded for former Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Rashan Gary and spent the 11th overall pick on safety Caleb Downs. Even a middle-of-the-road defense would be enough to put this team in contention, with Dak an outside MVP candidate and the Lamb-Pickens receiver axis as frightening as perhaps any in football.

It was a contrasting tale in Houston as DeMeco Ryans' Texans defense tormented the league while ranking No 1 in yards allowed, second in scoring and second in EPA/play. Will Anderson Jr and Danielle Hunter were unplayable up front, while Derek Stingley cemented his status as a premium lock-down corner at the core of a dogged, hard-nosed, suffocating unit that would led their side's route to the divisional round of the playoffs.

The attention turns to CJ Stroud amid contract negotiations with the quarterback, who threw four interceptions in the postseason loss to New England having not quite built on his emphatic rookie campaign as many had anticipated. The offensive line had been a contributing factor as one of Houston's glaring weaknesses, general manager Nick Caserio seeking to strengthen protection for Stroud by adding Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith and first-round rookie Keylan Rutledge. He also traded for running back David Montgomery as added juice to an attack ranked 18th in yards, and 22nd in rushing last season.

In another life Kyler Murray would/might/should be one of the most talked about epitomes of footballing escapism such is the talent of a quarterback joystick with the arm and wheels to wreak havoc. It has been nothing short of a slog and a disappointing chapter of irrelevance since the marquee contract featuring his widely-ridiculed homework clause in Arizona, but he enters the 2026 season as perhaps the most high-profile resurrection candidate.

Murray turned the page on his career this offseason as he signed with the Minnesota Vikings, teaming up with a head coach in Kevin O'Connell famed for his quarterback-whispering qualities, evidenced through Sam Darnold's career rebound.

Murray has swiftly ousted JJ McCarthy as the starting quarterback and will now take the reins on an offense led by the league's best receiver in Justin Jefferson, accompanied by a talented cast of Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and TJ Hockenson.

Murray is among the most intriguing case studies as he seeks to revive his career within the most gifted cohort of weapons and coaches he has experienced since being selected as the No 1 pick in 2019. That includes an 'X factor' of a defensive coordinator in Brian Flores who continues to roll out one of football's most inventive, full throttle, blitz-heavy units.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills: Joe Brady under pressure to lead Josh Allen to Super Bowl, says Phoebe Schecter
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter questions whether this could finally be the year one of Josh Allen or Joe Burrow win a Super Bowl; watch the Bills open their 2026 campaign against the Houston Texans live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm on Sunday as the race to Super Bowl 61 begins
articles.body:
The Bills renew their Super Bowl quest this season having endured more playoff agony earlier this year when they were beaten by the Denver Broncos in overtime of January's Divisional Round clash.

It had been deemed a premature end to one of their best opportunities yet to end prolonged Super Bowl agony, with Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs absent from the playoffs for the first time since 2014 and the likes of Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow also nowhere to be seen.

Sean McDermott was subsequently fired after nine campaigns in charge, with Brady being promoted to head coach from his post as offensive coordinator.

"Josh Allen will have had a say with Joe Brady coming in and taking on that role," said former Bills coach Schecter on Inside the Huddle .

"It was just odd at the time in terms of how it happened, that kind of firing in order to promote from within."

Allen's Bills have suffered four Divisional Round exits and two AFC Championship Game defeats since 2020, four of those losses coming against the Chiefs.

Their 73 victories in that period are notably more than any other team in the league, Allen consistently spearheading one of football's most potent offenses.

Buffalo sought to strengthen their quarterback's aerial options by trading for Chicago Bears wide receiver DJ Moore, who hasn't recorded a 1,000-yard campaign since 2023.

"You look at what DJ Moore does for the team when you bring him in," Schecter continued. "That already elevates an offense that has never really had a star receiver.

"They're still trying to keep that mentality, but you pair that with a fantastic running game. We saw James Cook all last season taking over, but it's a very interesting that we have so many teams in the AFC that were having a similar conversation around with your Lamar Jacksons, your Joe Burrows - when will these guys win a Super Bowl?

"That of all the teams the most pressure is on Joe Brady in terms of the expectation is for him to get to a Super Bowl because they've always been the bridesmaid, never the bride.

"It'll be fascinating to see how he manages that pressure, especially as they move deeper into the season. But everyone feels good about it. You've got a new stadium, you've got a new excitement around it and that kind of rejuvenation."

The Bills also hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator to oversee a new-look unit that saw the likes of Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White depart in the offseason.

"Leonard is the key to this whole deal," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold. "Jim Leonard is a brilliant young coach, and if he can get that defense just a little bit better than it's been and better balance, this could be Buffalo's year."

Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals stake their only claim as NFL 'nearly men' alongside both Allen's Bills and Jackson's Baltimore Ravens.

The Bengals have missed out on the playoffs for three straight years and managed just one postseason appearance since their defeat to the Los Angeles Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

Burrow, who has missed 16 games through injury over the last three seasons, demanded urgency from his team this offseason as he seeks to maximise, when healthy, one of the most explosive passing attacks in football.

"He said it himself, we all know he's been injured so many times coming into this season, or they've had some big injury within the team, but the time is now and they've got to chase that success," said Schecter.

"The biggest complaint last year was how they were putting so much money into this defense and they were probably the worst performing defense.

"But bringing in Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, you get Kyle Dugger from the Patriots, you've got a smart defense. You've got a safety who can now organise everybody.

"They've got to be able to go down and capitalise on having this fantastic trio on offense with Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and go attack it. This city needs it.

"The fan base are so desperate for it and you don't have an endless clock with Joe Burrow, especially seeing his injury rate over the past few seasons."

articles.title: NFL 2026 predictions: Super Bowl, MVP, offensive and defensive player of the year, best offseason addition and more
articles.summary: Who will win Super Bowl 61 at SoFi Stadium in February 2027? The 2026 NFL season gets under way this week as the Buffalo Bills face the Houston Texans from 6pm Sunday live on Sky Sports, followed by the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles
articles.body:
NDAMUKONG SUH: Caleb Williams, QB, Chicago Bears. Caleb is set up for a lights-out year. Heading into his third season, he's going to step up, play lights-out football, and really do his thing.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Lamar Jackson, QB, Baltimore Ravens. Lamar is going to be healthy and rejuvenated under Jesse Minter.

BRIDGET CONDON: Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Benglas. Joe Burrow has already shown us what he's capable of. Now his defense will finally be mediocre enough to give him his flowers. Burrow stays healthy and dominates his way back into the Super Bowl.

JASON BELL: Dak Prescott, QB, Dallas Cowboys. Dak will lead what could be the best offense in football as he feeds CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills. He's the best player in the league with a better supporting cast and now in Joe Brady an offensive-minded head coach.

CAM HOGWOOD: Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals. When I heard Joe Burrow's 'this is it' speech demanding urgency from his Bengals this offseason, I really believed him. Injuries have hindered him over the last three seasons, so too has a below-par defense hamstringing their chances of contending for a Super Bowl. But a healthy Joe Burrow, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at his disposal, is capable of torching any defense in football.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions . Jahmyr is going to be the focal point for Detroit - the true number-one option on that offense. As long as he stays healthy, he's going to put up elite, top-tier numbers.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Puka Nacua, WR, Los Angeles Rams. The Rams are going to unleash the NFL's best passing attack in 2026 and despite some off-field issues during this past offseason, there is no reason to believe that Puka Nacua's excellent level of play is going to drop off this season.

BRIDGET CONDON: Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals. Burrow is going to need some help. This offense is going to explode this season. The better Joe does, the better Ja'Marr plays.

JASON BELL: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions. The Lions are going to find a way to feed him the ball and make sure he gets explosive plays.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals. I've got a good feeling about the Bengals this season and Chase is a big reason why. With Zac Taylor dialling it up for Joe Burrow, Chase and co., the Bengals should be dynamic.

CAM HOGWOOD: Bijan Robinson, RB, Atlanta Falcons. When I look at the uncertainty around Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr at quarterback in Atlanta, it's hard not to feel like the entire Falcons operation rests on the shoulders of Bijan Robinson. He led the league in scrimmage yards last season and will deliver another huge return while spearheading Kevin Stefanski's offense.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Maxx Crosby, EDGE, Las Vegas Raiders. Maxx Crosby is coming back with a vengeance this year. He's heard all the outside noise and hype, and he's out to remind everyone who he is. He's an elite game-disrupter who just needed a quick chance to reset.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. The two-time Defensive Player of the Year was a wrecking ball in Cleveland last term and that was with the Browns holding very few leads where he could pin his ears back and attack. Teaming up with Aaron Donald, Garrett can complete the DPOY hat-trick.

BRIDGET CONDON: Aaron Donald, DE, Los Angeles Rams. It will be something out of a movie, retirement to DPOY. Aaron Donald will look everything like himself and more. People will be clawing to find out his retirement workout routine because he's coming back faster, stronger and even more dominant.

JASON BELL: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. With the Rams' offense, Myles Garrett is finally going to be able to close out games rushing the passer.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. You aren't in Cleveland anymore, Myles! Teams are going to have to throw to keep up, which translates to more sack opportunities. Trent McDuffie and a guy named Aaron Donald will make him even better.

CAM HOGWOOD: Will Anderson Jr, DE, Houston Texans. There was a great quote from Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins this offseason explaining how Anderson has reached a stage where he now realises his ability to "shut down practice" at any chosen moment, such has become of his dominance. I think we see that translate to live action games this Sunday. He established himself among football's game-changing disruptors last season while leading one of the most frightening defenses in the league. Myles Garrett will take some beating, but I think Anderson can be the man to pip him.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Mike McDaniel, offensive coordinator, Los Angeles Chargers. Mike McDaniel moving back into his absolute sweet spot as an offensive coordinator is huge. He has a phenomenal young talent in Justin Herbert, and McDaniel is going to take full advantage of dialing up creative schemes for him.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Jesse Minter, head coach, Baltimore Ravens. This is not meant to be disparaging to John Harbaugh, who was an excellent, Super Bowl-winning head coach during his 18 seasons in Baltimore. But a fresh start is probably best for everyone and I think Minter is going to improve the D and unleash a rejuvenated Lamar Jackson on the rest of the NFL.

BRIDGET CONDON: John Harbaugh, head coach, New York Giants. Harbaugh will lead the Giants to the NFC East title. He's just what New York needs to find their composure. Jaxson Dart isn't just an Abercrombie model - he's the next big thing. His time isn't this year but he's putting everyone on notice. He's coming.

JASON BELL: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. The same reason why he will win Defensive Player of the Year!

JEFF REINEBOLD: Jeremiyah Love, RB, Arizona Cardinals. We saw signs of how special he can be in preseason, but he's got to stay healthy behind an offensive line that is a work in progress.

CAM HOGWOOD: Sean Mannion, offensive coordinator, Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles may have won their division last season, but all was not well within one of the league's most uninspiring offenses, which endured something of an identity crisis under Kevin Patullo. His departure in the offseason prompted the appointment of former Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, who I think unlocks the best of Jalen Hurts with an exciting and revamped scheme on his way to head coaching contention.

NDAMUKONG SUH: The Minnesota Vikings win the NFC North. Everyone is hyped up on Detroit and Green Bay right now, but people are completely sleeping on Minnesota. They've got a fantastic head coach and great structure - they're the true dark horse in that division.

NEIL REYNOLDS: The Miami Dolphins take themselves out of the No.1 Draft pick stakes for 2027. The Dolphins have the youngest and arguably the worst roster in the NFL. But I think Malik Willis can produce just enough magic - to the dismay of ownership - to eliminate Miami from having the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, a position that could allow them to select their franchise quarterback of the future.

BRIDGET CONDON: The Tennessee Titans defense is going to be a lot better than people think. Robert Saleh has been part of nine top-10 defenses, and in his nine seasons as either a defensive coordinator or head coach, his teams finished top five in total defense five times. Saleh isn't going to let the Titans stay a joke.

JASON BELL: The Dallas Cowboys. Dak Prescott and co. will be in the Super Bowl conversation all year long.

JEFF REINEBOLD: The Cincinnati Bengals win the AFC North. Just a few stops a game and a turnover or two is all that is required, because the Bengals can score with any team in the league.

CAM HOGWOOD: From an individual perspective, Dallas Turner, while perhaps not a surprise to Vikings fans, is a name to keep an eye on. I think the third-year linebacker is a strong bet to establish himself among the leading pass rushers in the league and the face of Brian Flores' Minnesota Vikings defense following the departure of Jonathan Greenard. Here is his chance to break out as a complete and consistent threat up front to reach double figures in sacks. I think the Vikings as a whole could surprise some people and return to the playoffs behind a reinvigorated Kyler Murray.

NDAMUKONG SUH: The Los Angeles Chargers make the AFC Championship. The Chargers have every piece in place between their offensive coaching staff, Justin Herbert, and a tough defense. With Khalil Mack playing at an elite level, they're going to gel as a complete collective unit when it matters most.

NEIL REYNOLDS: The Rams struggle out of the gate. Despite a Week 1 win over the San Francisco 49ers, the Rams will follow their Australian adventure by losing three of their next four to Denver, Philadelphia and Buffalo. The biggest issues will be Davante Adams' swollen ankle after he gets bitten by a spider while Down Under and the confusing fact that Matthew Stafford picks up an Aussie accent he cannot shake until mid-October. The Rams will ride out their rough patch and still win the Super Bowl.

BRIDGET CONDON: The Steelers will have their first losing season since 2003 - Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy are going to show us why you never go back to your ex. It seems good in the moment, you remember all the good times you had. But... there was a reason you broke up. It wasn't working and it still wont work. The experiment will blow up by midseason. We'll be talking about a lot more than Bougnettes when the Saints upset the Steelers in Paris.

JEFF REINEBOLD: CJ Stroud bounces back and leads the Houston Texans to the AFC Championship Game. They have the best defense in a weak division and the stage is set for Stroud to get back to his former self.

CAM HOGWOOD: The New Orleans Saints win the NFC South and reach the playoffs for the first time since 2020 behind Tyler Shough, who proves to be Kellen Moore's answer at quarterback.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Denver Broncos to beat Chicago Bears. Denver takes it all home. Bo Nix is my pick for Comeback Player of the Year, and I have immense faith in a head coach like Sean Payton. He's already taken an elite group to the conference championship, and once Sean gets back to the Super Bowl stage, he's simply not losing it.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Los Angeles Rams to beat Baltimore Ravens. This could be a quarterback-led shootout with Matthew Stafford and Lamar Jackson trading blows. But those defensive closers in LA - Garrett and Donald - will ultimately make the difference in LA.

BRIDGET CONDON: Cincinnati Bengals to beat the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have it all - the coach, the quarterback, the defensive duo, the home-field Super Bowl advantage. It's too perfect! Life isn't a storybook ending so the Bengals are going to get their revenge. The Rams will score with time expiring in the fourth to make it 34-35. Sean McVay will try to go for two but Puka Nacua will drop the pass in the corner of the endzone to make the Bengals winners of their first Super Bowl.

JASON BELL: Los Angeles Rams to beat Denver Broncos. The Super Bowl will be all about defense - Myles Garrett and the Rams take it.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Los Angeles Rams to beat Buffalo Bills. Two of the league's best quarterbacks duel it out in SoFi Stadium. The Rams have always scored points and now have three of the best players in the league on defense in Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Trent McDuffie. Add the best coach in the NFL and you get the best team in football.

CAM HOGWOOD: Cincinnati Bengals to beat Los Angeles Rams. I'm an enormous Joe Burrow believe. I think he and the Bengals beat Matthew Stafford in a straight shoot-out, avenging their loss from Super Bowl LVI.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts and Jayden Daniels with questions to answer in NFL opener as Philadelphia Eagles roll out new offense
articles.summary: Watch Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles take on Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders from 9.25pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports NFL; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast throughout the season as Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold discuss the biggest storylines
articles.body:
The Eagles leaned heavily on Vic Fangio's star-studded defense alongside a sputtering Hurts-led attack on the way to winning the NFC East title last season.

It would culminate in a playoff defeat to the San Francisco 49ers and the firing of offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, while a disgruntled AJ Brown departed in the offseason after an apparent breakdown in his connection with Hurts both on and off the field.

"Only Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have accounted for more offensive touchdowns than Jalen Hurts in the last five years," said Reynolds on Inside the Huddle .

"He's a Super Bowl MVP, but those whispers about how he can impact the offense, how he gets along with his team-mates, all of that's grown about as loud as it's ever been during this offseason, about how he can run an offense, what he can do, what his limitations are."

Hurts was named Super Bowl MVP after a commanding performance to lead the Eagles to victory over the Kansas City Chiefs two years ago, denying Andy Reid's side a historic three-peat.

Still, doubts of his talents would follow amid a laboured 2025 campaign.

"It's hard, I think he can be a polarizing character at times because he's actually just so stoic throughout or almost maintains the same emotions. And people want to see him get happy or mad or anything like that," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter.

"I feel like there's so much of other people applying how they feel he should think or feel. Then you have people looking at his career in terms of criticising the run game, criticising his passing game, criticising who he throws the football to, and Philadelphia is not an easy place to play.

"We know that there's a lot of external pressure from the Eagles fans, whether you're winning or losing, but it feels like a team that has consistently been driven by what the outside noise wants, or maybe the coordinators are allowing that to happen where they think, 'oh, they think we need to pass it to this person, they think we should throw it'.

"It almost just needs all those doors shut, which is probably why Jalen Hurts is very much like that. Even spending time with him this offseason he pretty much is exactly the same. He doesn't really get too excited.

"It will be fascinating now, is it that addition by subtraction when it comes to AJ Brown, what does the offense look like?"

Hurts and the Eagles begin their season against another quarterback facing queries in the light of a disappointing campaign marred by injury.

Jayden Daniels missed 10 games for the Washington Commanders last season, failing to build on his Offensive Rookie of the Year-winning campaign.

"He told me in the summer he was going to learn to live to fight another down," said Reynolds. "I will believe it when I see it, once you get in the heat of the battle.

"There's a lot of questions about Jayden Daniels, because if he's healthy, let's not forget two seasons ago, they were in the NFC championship game against these very Eagles."

Schecter added: "Jayden Daniels is so fascinating because he does have such a slim fit frame and we've seen how that can have a negative impact, but we've also seen how his speed and athleticism has really helped the team at times is evasive moves in the pocket, or even just when he's scrambling or running down field.

"And then you've got on top of it, the amount of off-field work that he does from a preparation perspective. The extra meetings that he's doing in the morning to walk through the play script or the virtual reality that he's watching, not every quarterback does that.

"Its just making sure that his offensive line can protect him long enough against an Eagles defense and especially an Eagles defensive line that are just known for their aggression."

articles.title: Myles Garrett: Los Angeles Ram pass rusher to undergo surgery and miss at least four weeks after being placed on injured reserve
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams lose pass rusher Myles Garrett for at least the next month after placing the Defensive Player of the Year on injured reserve; Rams head coach Sean McVay says there is no timeline on the return of Garrett, who arrived in a trade from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason
articles.body:
The reigning Defensive Player of the Year was limited by the issue during training camp and admitted following Thursday's defeat to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne that it had proven more restrictive than first thought.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero was first to report the news on Sunday as the Rams prepare for an extended period without their marquee addition.

Garrett was traded to the Rams by the Cleveland Browns in the blockbuster deal of the NFL offseason, fresh from breaking the all-time single-season sack record in 2025.

"I don't really [have a timeline] yet," head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday. "It's all contingent upon how do things go today. You feel good about it.

"But I think it'd be unfair to him or really just without having the totality of all the information, to put any sort of timeline on it. We know that he'll be available in four weeks potentially, so we'll just take that a day at a time.

"Honestly, after I talked with him after the game, after I'd spoken with you guys and just seeing just how he felt. You look at it, we thought it was something that we'd be able to kinda manage. That wasn't necessarily the case.

"So having that evidence and being able to say, 'What's the next right thing?' It was right after the game, just in terms of listening to how he felt, how he was able to impact the game and even just, like, what you guys saw, with how limited we had to be with him. Obviously, we thought we were doing the right thing, but, in hindsight, you'll always be able to learn from it."

His arrival was followed by the shock return of Aaron Donald, who stunned the league by coming out of retirement to team up with Garrett at the forefront of the Rams' defense.

Donald was absent in Melbourne in Week One as he works his way back into full football shape.

Garrett is due to miss games against the New York Giants, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills over the next four weeks. The earliest Garrett would be eligible to return is against the Arizona Cardinals in Week Six.

articles.title: NFL Weekend Review: Josh Allen's box office finish, Trevor Lawrence's MVP contention and Derrick Henry greatness
articles.summary: The NFL Weekend Review guides you through the best of the action from across the league on the road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles; watch the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos in Monday Night Football, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.15 Tuesday
articles.body:
The Josh Allen experience is back with a vengeance. Perennial thrill, unyielding adventure, eternal tenterhooks - the knife-edge epitome of everything we've so dearly missed about this wonderful game called football.

The Buffalo Bills quarterback positioned himself front and centre to a box office finish on the NFL's opening Sunday of the 2026 season, flirting with catastrophe before playing hero just seconds later to lead his side to a 36-31 win over the Houston Texans.

Kamari Lassiter should have iced the game for Houston inside the final two minutes when Allen gift-wrapped a would-be interception to the Texans cornerback, who failed to hold onto the ball while back-pedalling in his own end zone. How quickly he learned not to grant Josh Allen a second life.

On the very next play Allen would connect with Joshua Palmer for a 34-yard touchdown on third-and-11 to put Buffalo on top with 1.36 remaining. Jim Leonhard's new-look Bills defense handled business from there, Greg Rousseau forcing a fumble from CJ Stroud and Terrel Bernard pouncing on the loose ball to call game in the final seconds.

The camera quickly panned to Allen's beaming smile on the sidelines as the Bills quarterback resumed the never-ending Super Bowl quest that continues to dictate the pre-season, in-season and, such has been his playoff agony, post-season narrative. Every year is his year, until it isn't, yet the vicious cycle never fails to convince us that his Lombardi lift is just around the corner.

It is moments like Sunday that reinforce the concept, Allen's association with the dramatic fuelling Buffalo's unwavering contention with him at the helm. The Texans had been purring with fresh optimism, their offence hanging in a shoot-out with what is consistently one of the league's best units, C.J. Stroud going toe-to-toe with Allen, until the latter had seen enough.

It is daggers like Sunday's, and closing moments like those, that define Allen - underlining an ability to strap a team to his back in a manner few other quarterbacks in the league can attest to. He is back like never before, piloting a side determined to cash in on his prime this offseason by firing Sean McDermott and subsequently replacing offensive coordinator Joe Brady with a new head coach.

Allen finished Sunday 20 of 29 for 334 yards and two touchdown passes to Palmer and newest receiver DJ Moore, while also rushing for two scores to lift his career tally of ground scores to 81.

The Bills are coming off their fourth divisional-round defeat in five years following January's loss to the Denver Broncos, having also been beaten at two AFC Championship Games since 2020. It stands as the NFL's biggest modern door-knocking venture. But Allen is back, and he just took down one of the most feared defenses in the league.

The Los Angeles Chargers remain one of the most frustrating teams in football, and flattered to deceive yet again as they began a season of promise in defeat. Jim Harbaugh's side fell to a 26-14 defeat to an Arizona Cardinals team led by Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, the early marriage of Justin Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel failing to generate the fireworks expected of it. Their depth at receiver beyond Ladd McConkey is unconvincing for a team with playoff ambitions and what had been a transformed defense under Jesse Minter feels short on game-changing pass rush disruptors.

The Chicago Bears have the offensive firepower to hurt and hang with the best in the NFL as Ben Johnson seeks to solidify his team as permanent Super Bowl contenders. Chicago scored their most points in a game since the 1980 season as they beat the Carolina Panthers 59-37 in the highest-scoring opening game in NFL history, in doing so amplifying their rising star quarterback and one of football's most dynamic rushing schemes. Caleb Williams reminded all of his credentials with a precision-perfect back-shoulder fade touchdown pass to Cole Kmet on his way to 269 passing yards and two scores, while D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both put up 100 yards rushing.

David Montgomery gives the Texans a new dimension. The question surrounding Houston heading into this season was whether CJ Stroud and their offense could reach a level capable of rewarding a Super Bowl-calibre defense. It proved it could be by going stride-for-stride with Josh Allen and the Bills, Montgomery shining with three touchdowns having arrived in a trade from the Detroit Lions in the offseason.

Bijan Robinson has a long season ahead. I'm not sure there is a more glaring example of an offense so heavily reliant on one player performing well in order to operate. Atlanta's quarterback problems are not going away anytime soon, you feel, and Sunday was an insight into how prominent Robinson will be in Kevin Stefanski's attack as he recorded 29 touches for 173 yards and a touchdown in scrimmage in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Trevor Lawrence is an MVP contender. Sure, the Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback was playing a poorly run Cleveland Browns team, and sure, he was facing a defence adjusting to life without Myles Garrett and Jim Schwartz. But there had been a sense coming into this season that the NFL still wasn't universally sold on the Lawrence-Liam Coen tandem. Based on Week One, Lawrence has picked up exactly where he left off at the end of a glittering second half to last season.

The former No 1 pick finished 18 of 23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns in Jacksonville's 34-10 victory, extending their winning streak to nine straight regular-season games dating back to the 2025 campaign. Coen continues to inspire the most assured, clinical and surgical version of Lawrence the NFL has seen.

Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg said his unit would be built on violence and bad intentions. That might have been an overreaction, because they barely got close enough to the Jags' play-caller to find out.

Dalton Kincaid : The Bills' tight end dazzled in a career-best performance in which he caught five of his six targets for a team-leading 130 yards, and came up with fourth-quarter catches of 40 and 35 yards respectively - an invaluable contribution to the Bills' thrilling win.

Jalen Hurts: The Eagles quarterback has his critics and will seemingly forever divide opinion over his place among the best quarterbacks in football, but it was Hurts who willed Nick Siranni's team to victory on Sunday. He wasn't pretty, nor was he perfect, but he showed his composure in the face of pressure once more to throw for three touchdowns in a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders.

Carson Wentz: This wasn't in the script. The Minnesota Vikings were forced into an early quarterback change against the Green Bay Packers when Kyler Murray exited with a concussion. In came Carson Wentz to lead Kevin O'Connell's offense, throwing for 133 yards and three touchdowns to stun the Packers in a 39-22 rout.

Baker Mayfield: Four days after signing a three-year, £121.9m contract extension with the Buccaneers, Mayfield fumbled the ball three times in his side's 33-27 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, including once in a scramble on the Bengals' one-yard line - a mistake that effectively cost his team the game in an encounter decided by a single score.

Cleveland Browns : The Browns' rebuild project has looked larger by the week - and their humiliating 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars further highlighted the size of the task at hand.

Quarterback Deshaun Watson - playing his first regular season game since October 2024 - was mediocre at best, his only touchdown coming in garbage time, and Cleveland's defence allowed Lawrence and his offence to score on six of their first seven drives.

Tennessee Titans : A home opener against an inexperienced New York Jets side was about the kindest fixture the Titans could have asked for to start their season - and even that proved too tall a task for the 2025 NFL's basement side. Head coach Robert Saleh fell victim to the side that sacked him in 2024, and 2025 No 1 pick Cam Ward failed to impress once again, managing just 140 passing yards.

Player of the Weekend - Derrick Henry, RB, Baltimore Ravens

The Baltimore running back - dubbed by team-mates and fans alike as 'King Henry' - added another regal flourish to his illustrious career with an incredible week one performance.

Henry notched 144 yards and three touchdowns from his 24 carries in the Ravens' 41-23 road drubbing of the Colts, moving him to third on the NFL's all-time rushing touchdowns list with 125, passing hall-of-famers Marcus Allen and Marvin Harrison.

At 32, Henry continues to redefine conventional ideas about his position, breaking records at an age that far surpasses the average running back's ability to continue playing in the NFL, let alone do it at the league-leading standard he performed at in the season opener.

History beckoned in both directions. The New Orleans Saints were threatening their biggest comeback win ever, and the Detroit Lions were threatening their biggest blown lead in franchise history having surrendered a 21-0 lead to find themselves locked at 24-24.

It would be Detroit who survived humiliation as they clinched a 31-30 win in overtime after Tyler Shough's pass fell incomplete on the two-point attempt.

Shough had sent the game to overtime with a nine-yard touchdown strike to Juwan Johnson with 1.07 remaining in the game, before the Lions struck in the extra period thanks to Amon-Ra St Brown's four-yard touchdown catch. But back came the Saints as Shough fired an eight-yard scoring strike to Noah Fant, before Kellen Moore elected to go for the win instead of the game-tying field goal.

Second-year quarterback Shough had been enduring a miserable start to his second before finishing 35 of 56 passing for 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions, Chris Olave his chief target with 10 catches for 182 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs, the highest-paid running back in NFL history, starred for the Lions with 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns.

The big news from Sunday came before kickoff as it was reported Myles Garrett will miss at least the next four weeks due to a knee injury that requires surgery.

The Los Angeles Rams pass rusher has been placed on injured reserve in an early disruption to his first season with the Rams after arriving in a blockbuster trade from the Cleveland Browns earlier this year.

Garrett was quiet on his debut for the team during the week as Sean McVay's side suffered a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne.

The Vikings were dealt an injury setback later in the evening when starting quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion in Minnesota's 39-22 win over the Packers.

The former Cardinals quarterback received a huge hit on a third-and-seven scramble in the first quarter, his helmet coming off as he came into contact with Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard. He eventually returned to his feet and was able to walk to the locker room, before being replaced by Wentz.

articles.title: New York Giants can make NFL playoffs with new John Harbaugh culture, says Jeff Reinebold
articles.summary: The New York Giants began their season with a divisional win over the Dallas Cowboys as they seek a return to the playoffs; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast throughout the season as Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold discuss the biggest storylines
articles.body:
Harbaugh took the reins on a coasting Giants organisation earlier this year after parting from the Baltimore Ravens following 18 seasons as head coach.

Awaiting him was a team of young talent seeking direction after just two winning seasons in the last 10 years, with Jaxson Dart inspiring fresh hope at quarterback alongside a pass rush tipped to join the league's elite units.

The first sign of Harbaugh's impact came in week one as the Giants beat their divisional rival Cowboys 28-20 after three touchdown passes from Dart, two of which went to Isaiah Likely, and a rushing score from Cam Skattebo.

"You're going to see the Harbaugh stamp on these Giants," Reinebold said on Inside the Huddle podcast. "The Giants in the last three or four years have been getting better, incrementally better.

"Harbaugh's staff didn't draft Jaxson Dart, they didn't draft Cam Skattebo, they didn't draft Malik Nabers. There's a bunch of good players in New York that they didn't draft.

"But what Harbaugh has done is he has created a culture in New York that's been lacking. Now you continue to build your roster as they have, and bringing in Isaiah Likely was a good move. If you're a Giants fan, you've got to really like the direction that this thing is going.

"It's not perfect yet. I don't think they're going to win their division. I do think they could be a playoff team."

An electric MetLife Stadium crowd would be treated to a hungry and driven team desperate to shake off the disfunctional cobwebs of predeceasing Giants outfits.

It marked their first week one home victory since 2010 and their first opening weekend win since 2022. Next up is a road trip to face the Los Angeles Rams following their loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne.

The Giants last reached the playoffs in the 2022 season when they finished third in the NFC East before beating the Minnesota Vikings on Wild Card weekend and eventually suffering a 38-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in the divisional round.

"What you see is a tougher team," Reinebold continued. "You see a team that plays with emotion, that the team that plays together.

"This will be the interesting, acid test to me. In the city with the most distractions in the world, the most newspaper outlets, the most media, can he keep them focused?

"They're just out of training camp. Now they're going out last night and everybody in New York is telling them how great they are.

"Can you keep them focused over the season? They're going to have to be if they're going to be a playoff team. That's going to be Harbaugh's test."
