articles.title: Patrick Mahomes returns from knee injury as Kansas City Chiefs storm past Denver Broncos
articles.summary: Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker stars on his Kansas City Chiefs debut with the most rushing yards by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles in 2012, posting 173 and two touchdowns; Walker signed with the Chiefs in free agency after guiding the Seattle Seahawks to Super Bowl glory
articles.body:
Mahomes did not appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, as he threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as AFC West division champions.

Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star, who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, also had three catches for 18 yards.

The Broncos, meanwhile, were abysmal on offense in their first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays.

Passing: Bo Nix, 17/28, 131 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: J.K. Dobbins, 8 carries, 36 yards

Receiving: Evan Engram, 4 catches, 43 yards, 1 TD

Passing: Patrick Mahomes, 15/27, 184 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT

Rushing: Kenneth Walker, 23 carries, 173 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: Travis Kelce, 3 catches, 71 yards

Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and the Broncos finished with 176 yards of offense, all despite the offseason splash they made by trading a package of draft picks to Miami for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.

Waddle had one catch for two yards, while Evan Engram led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards and their lone touchdown.

The big question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason programme and every practice of training camp, was how his surgically repaired left knee would hold up nine months to the day since he was hurt in a game against the Chargers. He erased any doubts when he capped the Chiefs' opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run.

It was Walker who did most of the running, though. The Super Bowl MVP for Seattle, who signed a three-year, $43.05m deal this offseason, had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half alone, along with a couple of catches out of the backfield.

The Broncos tied the game on Nix's 19-yard touchdown pass to Engram, but Walker carried the load as the Chiefs pieced together a 10-play, 80-yard drive late in the half. It ended when Mahomes found Rashee Rice, fresh off a knee injury of his own, and he caromed off a couple of Broncos defenders and into the end zone to make it 14-7 at the break.

Then it was Walker's turn to bounce off a defender, turning a fourth-and-one carry into a 60-yard touchdown run to start the third quarter.

The teams traded field goals later in the quarter thanks to big plays by each side: Brandon Jones intercepted Mahomes deep in Chiefs territory, setting up Wil Lutz's chip shot, and then Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 59 yards to set up Harrison Butker's field goal.

Nix's fumble on the ensuing possession allowed the Chiefs to put the game away.

Mahomes hit rookie running back Emmett Johnson on third down for a 26-yard gain, setting up first-and-goal at the Denver two. Andy Reid then turned to his bag of tricks as Mahomes lined up in a three-point stance alongside back-up QB Justin Fields, took the snap and shovelled the ball to Walker, who scooted untouched for the score.

Walker credited the presence of Mahomes as a contributing factor to his dazzling Chiefs debut as the Kansas City quarterback sought to reignite what has been a spluttering offense in recent seasons.

"They got to key on Pat. Pat's the best quarterback in the league," Walker said. "He makes the run game a lot easier."

Mahomes suffered a season-ending ACL and LCL injury last December before immediately undergoing surgery and dedicating the offseason to his recovery. Any questions over his mobility would be answered swiftly on Monday night by way of his 15-yard touchdown scurry.

"If I was going to say I was nervous for anything, it was getting hit on it," Mahomes said. "But I just wanted to play. I've done so much rehab and so much work to put myself in this position. I just wanted to play.

"This is what you do it for. My guys around me helped me. I didn't play my best football and we went out and beat a really good football team pretty well, and it's because the guys around me stepped up.

"It's just the start of it. We're still so early in the season. It's a great win but it's just Week One."

Head coach Reid hailed Mahomes as "phenomenal" as his team laid down an early statement after failing to win their division for the first time since 2015 last season.

"It was great to get Patrick back in the mix there, knock a little rust off," said Reid. "I was proud of him and how he handled it, and he ran the ball a couple of times, and your hat goes off to the guy. Phenomenal."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes could have done an Arne Slot and Liverpool but showed he is true champion, says Neil Reynolds.
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds hails "maniac quarterback" Patrick Mahomes as he starred on a winning return from last year's knee injury; the Chiefs began their season with a 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos after missing out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season
articles.body:
Their 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos was not only emphatic, it was encouraging on many levels. First of all, let's start with Patrick Mahomes.

This team is led by an absolute maniac at the quarterback position, and I mean that in a good way. Mahomes has a lot of Tom Brady in him, in that he's always on to the next thing. He's always attacking the next challenge.

If I think back to Tom Brady winning his seventh and final Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, I'm not really thinking about him standing under the confetti for the final time in his career. I'm thinking about the story that the next day he was on the phone to the Buccaneers trying to arrange his offseason workouts. He was already on to the next challenge.

That's what it takes to be a champion in the NFL, and not all sportsmen and sports leaders are like that. Take Liverpool two seasons ago when they won the Premier League. Arne Slot was in Ibiza partying and DJing, and the players were on yachts. How did that all turn out?

Mahomes is so driven and immediately opted for surgery after tearing his knee ligaments in mid-December. Then head coach Andy Reid told me in the summer, there was no offseason of holidays and time away from the facility. Mahomes was in the Chiefs facility for seven hours a day all through the offseason.

That's dedication. That's what it takes to get to the highest level of this game. The Chiefs were careful with Mahomes, getting the ball out quickly so he didn't take too many hits.

His average time to throw was 2.27 seconds. He didn't have a single drop back over four seconds, but he's also going to be putting his body on the line. He's the ultimate competitor.

On his touchdown run in the first half, he signalled to the NFL as he flexed his bicep in the end zone that he is back and ready to be as good as he's ever been. In fact, I won't use the word good with Patrick Mahomes, as great as he's ever been. When you look at how Mahomes was protected and operating, that leads to Andy Reid.

What a genius the Chiefs have as their leader and play caller. Getting the ball out of his quarterback's hands quickly, into the hands of the playmakers, and the short touchdown pass to Kenneth Walker in the second half was a thing of beauty. I don't think the Broncos knew who had the ball, who was running in which direction.

There were bodies flying everywhere. It looked like one of the battle scenes from a Star Wars movie. Kenneth Walker is a great addition to this team and they're going to lean heavily on him, so Mahomes doesn't have to do it all.

That's important because we look at Kansas City's wide receivers and do they have a standout one? Maybe not. Do they need one? Possibly not. Walker rushed for 173 yards and he finished with 191 yards from scrimmage.

The Chiefs also made plays on defense, showing that they are not going away on that side of the ball. Steve Spagnuolo lost some players on that side of football this season, but they always seem to scheme up advantages for their defenders. They're well led by Spagnuolo, they're physical and they make very few mistakes.

They held Denver to 176 total yards. That was their fewest since 2021. So lots of positives for the Chiefs.

It was great to see Mahomes back on the field on Monday night because the NFL is better when its biggest stars are in the midst of the action. But a warning for Denver moving forward and lots of work to do. I just mentioned the offensive failures, but the defense was atrocious.

They missed 28 tackles and there were 247 extra yards following those missed stops. That's the most for any defense in 2018. You know that is going to drive Sean Payton absolutely bonkers because he is a coach who preaches blocking, tackling and the fundamentals of football.

But this night belonged to the Chiefs and most of all it belonged to their maniac quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

articles.title: Justin Herbert: The NFL's most talented underachiever? Los Angeles Chargers quarterback tipped for greatness but facing more questions
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh last week suggested Justin Herbert would go down as the greatest quarterback in NFL history by the time he had finished his career - that was followed by a Week One defeat to the Arizona Cardinals as more questions about Herbert were raised
articles.body:
Herbert stepped out at SoFi Stadium as the best player on the field last weekend. He stepped off it having been out-duelled and outplayed by, with the greatest respect to him, everybody's favourite bridge quarterback in veteran Jacoby Brissett and a transitioning Arizona Cardinals team adrift of postseason discussion.

Brissett and a valiant defensive display had guided the Cardinals to a 26-14 opening weekend victory over Herbert's Los Angeles Chargers to pierce, but by no means burst (yet), the bubble of a team billed among the most exciting playoff contenders coming into Week One. Over-billed? Over-hyped? Time will tell.

It was the quintessential Chargers Chargering exhibition based on the discourse of recent years, a disjointed performance of mistakes and miscues negating the influence of superior individual talent. An all too familiar theme to this team.

Now, were you to drop somebody on earth for a day, ask them to watch a showreel of the NFL's starting quarterbacks and point out which they believed might be considered the best, the most feared, the most dangerous, you would bank on an initial eye test leading many to Justin Herbert. He remains something of a dream prototype blessed with the ludicrous arm talent, the marauding ground presence, the dwarfing stature, the fizzing needle-threading velocity and deep ball fireworks - as much, though, fuels most of the frustration surrounding his career thus far.

In his most successful moments, he has been spectacular, a match for any defense in the league and one of the most box office showcases in football. There has rarely been a flicker of doubt over his skillset, but noise-meets-uncertainty over both his killer instinct and credentials among the elite play-callers in the NFL is as loud as ever, you feel.

Herbert finished Sunday's loss 17 of 27 for 209 yards, one touchdown and an ill-informed interception while attacking double coverage downfield with 10 minutes to play and the Chargers trailing by nine. His day had started hot when he led an eight-play, 77-yard scoring drive including three passes for 60 yards to Ladd McConkey, whose exit with a chest injury after his touchdown catch before the end of the third quarter left Herbert and his offense short of answers.

In fact, the Chargers proceeded to go punt, turnover on downs, interception, turnover on downs, turnover on downs on the five possessions spent without McConkey, their offense failing to reach opposition territory in four fourth-quarter drives, while also collecting six of their team's total penalties including five in the second half and three straight on their penultimate series.

The performance came just days after head coach Jim Harbaugh forecast Herbert going down as the best to play his position.

"Allow me to call my shot, like Babe Ruth pointing his bat over to centerfield: Justin Herbert, when it's all said and done, when his career comes to an end, I predict he will be known as the greatest, best ever to play the position of quarterback," Harbaugh said. "When it's all said and done, and his career is finished, we're going to look back and say, 'Yep, that's the best that ever did it.'"

Harbaugh will not and should not change who he is, having become Herbert's most vocal and persistent cheerleader since taking over as head coach in 2024. He has repeatedly hailed his quarterback's potential for greatness and sought to speak Herbert's explosion into existence almost, but with it has come enlarged expectations and a Hollywood fishbowl feel. Is there such a thing as too much hype?

We might add that it is merely Week One, a prime window for premature panic. The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots both lost in the first week of last season before going on to reach the Super Bowl, while the widely favoured Los Angeles Rams were just beaten by the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne; nobody wrote them off, nor is anybody writing them off. Seasons aren't defined in Week One, but an unwelcome start has only prompted further question marks.

Part of the intrigue around Herbert this season comes from the hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, whose wizardry fell flat in a disappointing end to his Miami Dolphins head coaching tenure but has seen his arrival tipped to unlock the best of his quarterback's alien arm. The best of McDaniel's offense in Miami relied on Tua Tagovailoa's quick-release passing concepts, heavy pre-snap motion and a dynamic rushing attack off which his quarterback could tee, so Herbert will be asked to stray from his comfort zone a little. Every quarterback-coordinator marriage needs time to flourish, McDaniel similarly seeking to justify his own advertising as one of the most influential offensive figureheads in modern football.

McDaniel failed to get his running game going at all through second-year back Omarion Hampton, who managed just 43 yards from 12 carries and averaged only 1.5 yards before contact behind an offensive line that surrendered three sacks. It had been an area the Chargers appeared to address efficiently over the last two seasons under Greg Roman, whose run-heavy offense restored some long-lost stability to their attack. No balance, no party.

Herbert was sacked 54 times last season, the second-most in the league, as the Chargers went without two-time Pro Bowl left tackle Rashawn Slater for the entire campaign while losing Pro Bowl right tackle Joe Alt for 11 games through injury. His 225 sacks and 615 hits entering the season marked the most on any quarterback since Herbert was drafted with the sixth overall pick in 2020. Both Slater and Alt returned this weekend, but weaknesses continued to show on the interior of the Chargers' offensive line.

The numbers have often spoken to his ability to join the NFL's premier quarterbacks at the table. Herbert's 24,820 passing yards through his first six seasons are the second most in NFL history behind only Peyton Manning, whom he surpassed for the most completions by a quarterback in his first six seasons.

He also previously began his NFL career by setting the record for most consecutive 4,000-yard passing seasons with three in a row from 2020 to 2022 behind his best offensive arsenal featuring Keenan Allen, Mike Williams and Austin Ekeler. The gradual departure of the aforementioned trio hasn't helped; McConkey, Quentin Johnston and tight end David Njoku are now his most recognised pass-catching targets.

But for all his stats through the air, the one number Chargers fans care about is playoff wins, which currently stands at zero from three postseason appearances. Herbert has fallen in the Wild Card round in three of the last four years, witnessing the Chargers blow a 27-0 lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2022 playoffs, producing a career-worst 43.8 completion percentage and four interceptions against the Houston Texans in the 2024 playoffs and throwing for just 159 yards and no touchdowns while being sacked six times against the Patriots last season.

There is something to be admired about the ability for Herbert to become one of the prized faces of the league without quite yet managing to break through the glass ceiling. For the purposes of further fuelling an AFC arm's race brimming with quarterback talent, football is urging and willing him on to thrust himself among the perennial frontrunners, and football knows he is capable of doing so.

But games like that of Sunday should not be happening. Year seven is up and running and the Justin Herbert story remains both captivating and impossible to forecast.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills beat Detroit Lions 41-31 in first match at Highmark Stadium as Josh Allen stars again
articles.summary: The Bills christened their $2.1bn Highmark Stadium with an impressive win over the Lions; Star quarterback Josh Allen starred once more with his fourth career five-touchdown performance; watch Week Two of the NFL season on Sky Sports, with five matches live on Sunday
articles.body:
It was Allen's fourth career five-TD outing, and followed a four-touchdown outing (two passing, two rushing) in Buffalo's 36-31 season-opening win at Houston.

The $2.1bn stadium that officially opened last month was built across the street from the Bills' former home.

Allen followed the pre-game fireworks celebration with more fireworks of his own by overseeing touchdown drives on each of Buffalo's first four possessions.

He scored the first regular-season TD in the stadium on a 1-yard run 5:51 into the opening quarter. He followed that with a 43-yard scoring pass to a wide-open Josh Palmer. Tight ends Dalton Kincaid, with a 16-yard catch, and Dawson Knox, with a 1-yarder, also scored for Buffalo in the first half.

Allen finished 20 of 31 for 248 yards, and added 72 yards rushing. James Cook had 134 yards rushing and put the game away with a 1-yard TD run with 2:50 left.

Allen's two rushing TDs upped his career total to 83, moving him into a tie for 18th on the NFL list with Jim Taylor. He also picked up his 90th regular-season victory, in becoming one of just four quarterbacks to reach that milestone through their first nine seasons.

The Lions were undone by an injury depleted defense, and a banged-up offensive line that had difficulty opening holes for Jahmyr Gibbs and protecting Jared Goff.

After rallying from a 21-0 deficit to cut Buffalo's lead to 34-24, the Lions offense stalled midway through the fourth quarter. Backed up at their own 10, the Lions went three-and-out and forced to punt after Goff had two passes tipped by Deone Walker, and Gibbs was stopped for no gain.

Goff finished 26 of 38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns, with Amon-Ra St. Brown having nine catches for 142 yards and two scores. Gibbs also scored on an 11-yard catch but was limited to 52 yards rushing. Sam LaPorta also scored on a 1-yard catch.

St. Brown and Gibbs have now scored in the same game 22 times to move into a tie for fourth place in matching the Cleveland receiver/running back combo of Paul Warfield and Leroy Kelly.

The Lions' defense got off to a dreadful start in allowing Bills to score 27 points and gain 299 yards in the first half alone.

The struggles carried over from a season-opening 31-30 overtime win over New Orleans, in which the Saints rallied from a 21-0 first-half deficit and lost only after their 2-point conversion failed in overtime.

The Lions troubles began on Buffalo's second drive when two defenders converged on DJ Moore in the flats and allowing Allen to find Palmer wide open deep for a 43-yard touchdowns. On Buffalo's next drive, a holding penalty against Rock Ya-Sin, negated Skyler Gill-Howard's interception of a tipped pass.

The Lions' offense had its own sputters, with Goff sacked twice and also having a snap go over his head on Detroit's first two series.

articles.title: NFL Gameday Preview: Caleb Williams predicts 'bad things' as Chicago Bears meet Minnesota Vikings in Mexican standoff between Ben Johnson and Brian Flores
articles.summary: Watch the Chicago Bears against the Minnesota Vikings live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm Sunday, followed by the Denver Broncos against the Jacksonville Jaguars before the Kansas City Chiefs face the Indianapolis Colts in Sunday Night Football from 1.20am Monday.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson's full-throttle free-scoring Chicago Bears offense hosts Brian Flores and his blitz-frenzied Minnesota Vikings defense. A multi-layered attack built on motion, savvy diagnosis-meets-adjustment and funky formations consistently challenging convention. And a Flores resistance that functions on personnel versatility, weak-spot detection and pressure from all areas of the field.

It is the ultimate chess match of fearless coaches, whose well-established systems and approaches by now grant them the freedom to shred anticipatory gameplans with the proverbial slow ball. Both run systems dictated by immediate personnel and coverage diagnosis; miss one tiny detail and you are already dead.

The Bears just put up 59 points and 552 yards of offense in their Week One victory over the Carolina Panthers 100-yard rushing games from D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, both of whom scored twice on the ground, alongside two rushing touchdowns from Caleb Williams. Flores and the Vikings meanwhile sent the blitz on 73.8 per cent of Jordan Love's dropbacks during Minnesota's 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers, the highest rate a quarterback has been blitzed since 2023.

"It's a game-plan defense, he's gonna game plan from first snap to last snap," said Bears quarterback Williams. "Coach calls this 'mental war' when you go against him. That's what it is. Bad things are going to happen, you've got to be able to fight back and stay steady.

"That's one of the biggest things is not allowing his defense and all of that to fluster you and get in your mind. You stay steady and now it's time to go make plays and get completions and when the big ones show up, take them and find them."

Johnson, without even trying to, delivered the perfect advert for the game during an exchange with a reporter during his press conference earlier in the week.

The reporter was in the process of asking the Bears head coach as to whether there was the risk of overthinking and pre-empting when it came to the task of planning for a Flores defense. It prompted a widening grin that alone would sell the story of this weekend's matchup.

"Yeah, yeah, yes, there is," he laughed.

In reply to the follow-up question, he joked he was already stuck "in that path" of overdoing how he would tackle Flores this time.

"There's a lot of that. Our guys, I want them to go out and play fast. I want to make sure we're sound… making sure we have a hat for a hat as often as we can. And if he gets us on something then that's fine. We gotta come together and make sure we get it corrected and we'll move on from there."

Johnson arrives 5-1 in matchups against Flores' Vikings defense across his time as both Detroit Lions offensive coordinator and Bears head coach. He has won one and lost one with Chicago, Flores laying out completely contrasting performances in both, adopting his blitz-heavy approach on one occasion and electing to drop multiple men into coverage on the other in a test of Williams' field read. His ability to jump from one extreme to the other is largely unmatched in football and creates one of the ultimate challenges for a young offense.

Minnesota Vikings @ Chicago Bears - 6pm - LIVE on Sky Sports NFL: As the Vikings bid farewell to Jonathan Greenard in the offseason, expectations naturally heightened around Dallas Turner to make his leap as the new face of Kevin O'Connell's pass rush. He made a lightning start in Week One with one sack, 10 pressures, seven quarterback hits and a forced fumble against the Packers; he thrives on speed, explosiveness and agility more so than sheer power off the edge, as much plus lane discipline required against a shape-shifting Bears defense designed to thwart players like him. At the heart of Chicago's offense lies Williams, who is coming off his own statement performance in Week One perhaps best defined by his stunning back-shoulder fade touchdown pass to Cole Kmet. He also went some way towards answering lingering questions of his accuracy with a completion percentage upwards of 72; sure, it was the Panthers, but the early signs of him joining the elite were good.

Pittsburgh Steelers @ New England Patriots - 6pm - LIVE on Sky Sports Football: The attention returns to Drake Maye as the New England Patriots quarterback seeks to kickstart his season after tossing three costly, wildly ill-guided interceptions in the fourth quarter of his side's opening day defeat to the Seattle Seahawks. The game-icing pick to Josh Jobe in the end zone was a staggering miscue for a player that was so often rewarded for his aggression during the 2025 campaign; he will also remain without new star weapon AJ Brown after he was placed on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. The Steelers look to go 2-0 after opening their campaign with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, during which Aaron Rodgers began the final game of his farewell season 24 of 40 passing for 221 yards and a touchdwon.

Jacksonville Jaguars @ Denver Broncos - 9.05pm - LIVE on Sky Sports NFL & Sky Sports Main Event: The Denver Broncos were the No 1-ranked defense in the NFL last season, leading the league with 68 sacks behind Nik Bonitto. They were a shadow of that unit in Week One as they missed 28 tackles for 247 extra yards - the most by any defense since 2018, as noted by my colleague Neil Reynolds. This version of Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen's offense would like a piece of that action having just torn apart the Cleveland Browns in a four-touchdown performance from the Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback, including a truly special demonstration of needle-threading anticipation to Josh Cameron.

Seattle Seahawks @ Arizona Cardinals - 9.25pm - LIVE on Sky Sports + (stream): Backup Drew Lock will start at quarterback for the Super Bowl champion Seahawks after replacing Sam Darnold following his injury in the opening drive of their opening-day win over the Patriots. Lock, who is 10-18 as a starter, completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown last week, reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba accounting for 122 yards through the air. The Cardinals are coming off their Week One win over the Los Angeles Chargers, which saw first-year coach Mike LaFleur became the first non-interim coach to win his first game as coach of the Cardinals since Don Coryell did it in 1973. Trey McBride remains the leading threat for Arizona on offense, while Uchenna Nwosu was everywhere on the field in a rampant performance against the Patriots.

Washington Commanders @ Dallas Cowboys - 9.25pm - LIVE on Sky Sports Football:

The Dallas Cowboys defense remains a pressing concern for a team with the offensive arsenal to hurt any side in football. Led by new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, they just shipped 28 points against Jaxson Dart and the New York Giants as familiar weaknesses to their pass rush proved costly once again. Dallas added veterans Rashan Gary and Von Miller to their pass rush in the offseason, while Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark had been expected to upgrade the Cowboys' defensive front since their arrival, but the Week One signs were discouraging against a Giants offense still finding its way. Both teams feature potential stalwarts on defense in Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles and Cowboys safety Caleb Downs as the former Ohio State teammates and fellow first-round draft picks reunite.

Indianapolis Colts @ Kansas City Chiefs - 1.20am Monday - LIVE on Sky Sports NFL & Sky Sports Main Event: The workhorse running backs are coming. Jonathan Taylor reminded all that he is THE Indianapolis Colts offense last weekend as he rushed 19 times for 98 yards yards and two touchdowns in their defeat to the Baltimore Ravens. Kenneth Walker III meanwhile teased his potential game-changing impact as the newest field-tilting star of the Kansas City Chiefs offense, rushing for 173 yards and a 60-yard touchdown alongside three catches for 18 yards and a score in their 31-10 win over the Broncos. He looks the perfect tool with which to help Patrick Mahomes ease back in following his knee injury and reignite what has been a stagnant Chiefs offense in recent seasons.

Rams head coach Sean McVay on his side's loss in Melbourne : "It's almost like you try to do the Men in Black thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago. We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

Titans QB Cam Ward: "I think I am a very good quarterback. I think I do a lot of things different, that a lot of quarterbacks can't do. And there's also stuff I have to get better at, some things that I lack and that's a process you take on each and every day."

Seahawks QB Drew Lock: "I would say if there's one thing I'm saying to myself, it's take care of the football and get it into these guys' hands."

Vikings QB Carson Wentz on WR Justin Jefferson: "The guy's so good. He's the best in the world at what he does, and sometimes you've just got to give him a chance. When it goes his way he usually finds a way to come down with it."

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel on the Steelers: "I think the Steelers is the identity. The Steelers are going to be the Steelers. They're big and they're long and they're going to try to force the quarterback into making mistakes."

Vikings safety Harrison Smith on Bears QB Caleb Williams: "He's obviously capable of making highlight play after highlight play. He's really got it all. He's extremely talented. He's operating that offense very well."

The Cowboys haven't started 0-2 since 2010, when Wade Phillips was fired as coach with a 1-7 record as Dallas went on to a 6-10 finish.

T.J. Watt's late pick-six for the Steelers against the Falcons saw him join Hall of Famer Julius Peppers as the only players in NFL history to have 100 sacks and 10 interceptions.

Tennessee's Anthony Hill Jr. recorded 16 total tackles in Week One, the most of any player in his NFL debut within the last 30 years.

Aaron Rodgers has thrown multiple touchdowns in six consecutive starts against New England.

The Jaguars have won nine straight regular season games dating back to last season, outscoring opponents by 177 points during the streak, the highest point differential over a nine-game span by any team since the Bills had +179 from Week 16, 2020-Week 8, 2021.

Houston's Will Anderson Jr has 93 QB pressures since the start of last season - second most in the league - with 40 happening in under 2.5 seconds.

The Dolphins were tied for the most sacks allowed last week with five and were one of five teams, along with the 49ers, to have no sacks in the opener.

The Vikings have won six straight games at Soldier Field, one short of the franchise record for consecutive road wins over a division opponent. They won seven straight at Detroit from 1968-74 and seven straight on the road against Green Bay from 1971-77.

articles.title: Union Jack Classic: Kansas Jayhawks to face Arizona State Sun Devils in college football's debut at Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: The Kansas Jayhawks face the Arizona State Sun Devils in the inaugural Union Jack Classic at Wembley Stadium on Saturday; watch Week Two of the NFL season on Sky Sports, with five matches live on Sunday
articles.body:
Football is no stranger to international expansion having seen the NFL host regular-season games in London since 2007, while Ireland serves as the home of the annual College Football Classic at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

In fact, college football spread its wings long before now having also previously played games in Tokyo and Milan in the 1980s, as well as famously heading to Tanzania for the 2011 Kilimanjaro Bowl.

From its staple marching bands to its iconic tailgates to its deep-rooted family tribalism, the college game is now primed to showcase its unique make-up with the inaugural Union Jack Classic.

"I think I've probably had fish and chips four times since I've been here so it's been a nice culture shock," says Arizona State punter Nick McLarty.

McLarty is perhaps more accustomed to a change in environment more so than any player arriving in the UK this week having grown up in Melbourne, Australia, the 6ft 7in punter having started out playing Aussie Rules before turning his talents to a different kind of football.

"It's my first time coming to London," he said." It's funny, I was on the phone with mum before and actually didn't tell her so the first time she found out was this morning. It's been a lot of fun.

"I have a brother who is pretty big into soccer and when he found out I was playing at Wembley he was beside himself and it's been fun going round to Buckingham Palace.

"The people and the accent [has been a nice change], I've been so used to the American accent, it's been a nice touch of reality for what the rest of the world is like to be able to speak to other people."

Wembley is expected to welcome 60,000 fans this weekend as both teams arrive 1-1 on the season, Kansas coming off a 38-21 defeat to Missouri on Friday night and the Sun Devils having just lost 48-20 to Texas A&M.

For many of the players it represents their first time leaving the US, Kansas head coach Lance Leipold having described it as a "lifetime" opportunity.

Leipold had notably been a graduate assistant for Wisconsin when the Badgers featured in the Coca-Cola Classic in Tokyo back in 1993.

"[That] is when you really get to think about what you did, and something that you talk about with your friends and team-mates for a lifetime. And that's partially what I'm hoping for," Leipold said this week.

"I think even though we have so many things going on in college athletics, that we should not take away experiences such as this if they're afforded to you, and try to make the most of it. I think it's something that we're looking forward to."

The pre-game tailgate is scheduled to kickstart festivities at 10am along Wembley Way, with 15,000 fans flying over from the US to contribute to what is hoped to be a classic college football atmosphere.

"I grew up playing soccer, one of my old coaches who played for Everton always talked about playing at Wembley and scoring a goal there so it's kind of a full circle moment really," said Sun Devils defensive lineman Zac Swanson.

"It's super cool and we're really blessed to be here. It took a little bit to get adjusted to the time, it's probably one of our better weeks because back in Arizona it's 115 degrees out and now we get to practise in 70s so preparation is going very well.

"It's almost like a whole culture shock because it's so different. My favourite thing is the houses and environment, you see the soccer pitches everywhere, we don't really have that in the US."

Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III will be in London as part of the Fox Sports team presenting live their pre-game show live from the UK.

He explained what makes college football's atmosphere and environment special.

"The fandom around college football is better," he told media. "It just is. The traditions and all that stuff are definitely more deep-rooted. The rivalries are better than the NFL rivalries and I just think it adds to it.

"There is no NFL without college and there's no college football without the NFL.

"You actually sink your roots deeper into the ground by becoming a college football fan so you can truly follow these guys," Griffin said. "That jersey that you put on, that you buy, that you spend all your hard-earned money on actually means more to you because you've been following those players longer."

articles.title: Mike Vrabel when asked about Drake Maye's game vs. Steelers: 'You're not going to ruin my Sunday'
articles.summary: As the Patriots face a tougher schedule, the question will linger: Have defenses gotten a bead on the blueprint to handle Maye? Are the Patriots simply facin...
articles.body:
Back at 1-1 thanks to a defense that thoroughly outmatched the Pittsburgh Steelers' offense , New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed concerns.

His offense had net 327 yards and 13 points one week after 285 and 10. With the Patriots' defense strip-sacking Aaron Rodgers and returning the takeaway for a touchdown, New England won 20-3.

So when Vrabel was asked whether he is concerned about quarterback Drake Maye and the Patriots' offense, he revealed a bit of chippiness.

"Nope, just trying to win the game," he told the Boston Globe reporter who asked. "You're not going to ruin my Sunday, but I'll come back to you tomorrow. Thanks, bud."

Another reporter began to ask a question about Maye.

"You neither," Vrabel interrupted. "You're not going to ruin it, either."

Vrabel was correct that as head coach, his top job is to lead his team to victory, which the Patriots accomplished against a Steelers team that never found its way to the end zone.

Yet Vrabel's disinterest in publicly unpacking offensive inconsistencies varied dramatically from Maye's remarks.

"Yeah, definitely not where we want to be …" Maye began his postgame statement. "[We did] little things that just hurt ourselves, and it's going to end up coming back to bite us. So it already bit us once last week. So our defense [was] playing great, and shout out to — fun watching them play.

"We got to match it and have more urgency, and [it] starts in practice."

Maye completed 14 of 22 pass attempts for 208 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception Sunday. He rushed four times for another 17 yards.

The game was cleaner than Maye's season opener, in which he threw three interceptions in a 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . But as Maye, even if not Vrabel, acknowledged: The Patriots' offense looks far less rhythmic than it did a year ago, when Maye's MVP runner-up campaign helped the Patriots to a Super Bowl berth.

So while he's not — and shouldn't — panic about the gaps in cohesion, Maye knows the Patriots' offense can't settle for what it has shown so far this season.

"You got to be excited and enjoy the win," Maye said. "But at the same time, you realize that playing like this isn't going to end up with offensively us leading our team to wins. …

Patriots limited to one offensive touchdown vs. Steelers

Perhaps the most helpful unit for Maye on Sunday was the Steelers' offense.

Aaron Rodgers' unit converted on just two of 12 third downs and made the Patriots' errors less costly.

When running back Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble in the first quarter, the Steelers responded with a three-and-out that let the Patriots off the hook. When Maye was nailed for a sack on a Jalen Ramsey blitz in the first quarter, Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith 's defensive offside penalties negated the loss.

And after running back TreVeyon Henderson missed the season opener due to an ankle injury, the second-year Patriot returned Sunday to rip off a 39-yard touchdown aided by a DeMario Douglas downfield block.

"TreVeyon's touchdown had everybody blocked up," Maye said. "Pop made a huge block, and you just see the extra effort when it works. And when we strain a little bit harder, good things happen."

No more offensive touchdowns came in the 53 minutes that followed.

Instead, Maye took three sacks on the day, had four passes batted and sailed a 23-yard pass short of tight end Hunter Henry . Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen intercepted it instead.

"I just got to give him a chance farther with the linebacker kind of panicking back, but at the same time, I can get it underneath and keep the drive going once we get into that almost high red-zone area," Maye said of the interception he threw 33 yards from the end zone. "Trying to take a shot and kind of hit one, but at the same time, got to know that that's not always the time to take a shot on first down."

The early third-quarter pass left Patriots fans wondering if another unraveling, a la the blown lead vs. Seattle a week prior, was pending. A stalled drive that led to a missed field goal continued those questions. But the Steelers failed to score off either error, setting up Maye's best move of the day.

Escaping the pocket to his right with 2:12 to play in the third quarter, he hit receiver Romeo Doubs 47 yards down field, and Doubs took the pass another 16 yards before completing the 63-yard play.

"Obviously great play-call by our OC," Doubs said. "DBs guess in this league, and I had leverage, and it was just a great ball, great catch situation."

The Patriots still finished the drive with only a field goal, but their lead was widening, and a scoop-and-score strip sack of Rodgers awaited from their defense.

"You have to affect the quarterback each and every week, and we have to do a better job and continue to do a good job of helping our quarterback be efficient," Vrabel said. "And he has a large part in that, but we know that that's the formula."

Maye's production wasn't the top force carrying the Patriots to Sunday's win. But he also didn't detract from that goal, as he blamed himself for doing the prior game.

"I can only imagine what it's like being a quarterback in the National Football League," said Vrabel, who played 14 years as an NFL linebacker. "And so again, he's the one that's going to orchestrate and conduct everything that we do and make sure that everybody believes that the play that we're running is going to be the one that's successful. And not every time it is. But he has to be able to take that demeanor and spread it to the football team, throw to the guy that's open, and again, make great decisions.

"I'm always going to trust his decision."

Some of Maye's sacks reflected a lack of open receivers downfield, not unrelated to his top receiver A.J. Brown landing on injured reserve due to a high ankle sprain. Maye also lost his right guard, Mike Onwenu, to injury at the end of the first quarter, shuffling an already-shuffled-from-last-year offensive line.

It's common for NFL teams to need multiple weeks early in the season to develop a rhythm. So perhaps long-term concern about Maye is not warranted. But in the short term, the Patriots' production has dipped from last year's prolific season. Maye's accuracy and reputation for mistake-free football have slipped since December.

Maye tossed just eight interceptions, compared to 31 touchdowns, in 17 regular-season games last season. In four playoff games and two 2026 regular-season games since then, he has thrown eight picks.

After losing three fumbles in the regular season last year, he lost seven in the playoffs.

So as the Patriots face a tougher schedule, the question will linger: Have defenses gotten a bead on the blueprint to handle Maye? Are the Patriots simply facing more difficult opponents than their light schedule last season? Perhaps both elements are relevant.

Vrabel, as he said, will "come back to [that] tomorrow." On Sunday, he was more interested in celebrating returning to .500 ahead of games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Buffalo Bills , each of whom won their opener after making a playoff appearance last season.

Doubs, who caught the 63-yard pass a week after a nationally televised drop, said his team will keep improving.

"I thought our jump from last game to this game was much improved," he said. "I look forward to finding ways to get better moving forward."

articles.summary: NFL News: Jayden Daniels is facing another worrying chapter in his young NFL career after suffering an elbow injury against the Dallas Cowboys on September 20, .
articles.body: Jayden Daniels is facing another worrying chapter in his young NFL career after suffering an elbow injury against the Dallas Cowboys on September 20, 2026. The Washington Commanders quarterback was carted off the field after hurting the same left elbow that sidelined him twice last season. With his injury history growing, Daniels' latest setback raises fresh questions about his recovery and the team's approach to his return.Jayden Daniels' elbow injury history dates back to 2025Daniels first injured his non-throwing elbow on November 2, 2025, during a Sunday Night Football matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. The injury came during an already difficult season, as the young quarterback had missed time with knee and hamstring problems.The elbow dislocation forced Daniels out of the game, with Marcus Mariota stepping in at quarterback. Initial reports offered some hope, as the injury appeared to involve limited damage. Since it affected his left arm rather than his throwing arm, Daniels had a chance to return sooner.He missed three games before making his comeback against the Minnesota Vikings. However, that return did not last long.On December 7, 2025, Daniels aggravated the same elbow after landing hard on it during an interception return. Although he avoided another dislocation, Washington decided to shut him down for the rest of the season.The decision came after a campaign marked by several injuries, leaving the Commanders without their young quarterback for a significant stretch.Jayden Daniels suffers another elbow injury against CowboysDaniels' latest injury occurred at the end of the first half against Dallas on September 20. The quarterback stumbled backward after being stepped on and extended his left arm to brace his fall.The impact appeared to force his elbow into an awkward position, raising concerns about a possible dislocation or hyperextension. Daniels was visibly in pain and needed a cart to leave the field.The injury's severity has not been confirmed in the provided report. However, the fact that it involves his non-throwing arm could be a factor in determining his recovery timeline.Washington will also have to weigh the urgency of getting Daniels back on the field against the risk of another setback. His 2025 return, followed by a second injury to the same elbow, offers a clear reason for caution.For now, Daniels' latest injury adds another challenge to a career that has already seen too much time spent on the sidelines. articles.title: Inspiring story on determination: How Patrick Mahomes overcame months of pain and uncertainty to chase another Super Bowl
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has spent years proving he can deliver when the pressure is highest. Yet his toughest test did not come in a playoff game. It began wi.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has spent years proving he can deliver when the pressure is highest. Yet his toughest test did not come in a playoff game. It began with a serious knee injury that forced him away from football and into a long, demanding recovery. For the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback, the dream of another Super Bowl required a different kind of fight, one measured in patience, pain and daily sacrifice.Patrick Mahomes’ knee injury changed everything for the Chiefs quarterbackMahomes’ 2025 season ended in painful fashion. On December 14, he tore the ACL and LCL in his left knee during a game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The injury required surgery the following day, leaving the Chiefs without their star quarterback for the remainder of the campaign.For a player whose game relies on movement, balance and quick reactions, the road back was never going to be simple. Mahomes had to put aside the familiar rhythm of practices, game preparation and competition. Instead, his days became centred on recovery, with each step forward depending on careful work and medical guidance.The timing made the setback even harder to accept. Kansas City had endured a difficult 2025 season, finishing 6-11 and missing the playoffs. Mahomes could not simply turn the page and prepare for another game. First, he had to rebuild the strength and mobility in his injured knee.The challenge was not just physical. Elite athletes are used to controlling their preparation and pushing themselves to the limit. Rehabilitation demands a different mindset. Progress can feel slow, and doing too much too soon can create new problems.Mahomes had to trust the process, even when his competitive instincts urged him to move faster.Patrick Mahomes embraced months of demanding rehabilitationMahomes began his recovery with one clear target: return for the opening week of the 2026 NFL season. When he addressed reporters in January, he remained hopeful but realistic about the work ahead.“It's a long process, but I'm excited for it.”The statement reflected a mindset built around the next step rather than the finish line. Mahomes knew that wanting to play was not enough. He needed to meet medical checkpoints, regain strength and allow his body to heal at the right pace.He also acknowledged that his doctors sometimes had to hold him back because he wanted to do more. That detail offered a glimpse into the discipline required during recovery. For Mahomes, sacrifice meant not only pushing through difficult sessions, but also accepting when restraint was necessary.Chiefs head coach Andy Reid later revealed that Mahomes was spending around seven hours a day at the team’s facility working on rehabilitation. Assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer helped guide his recovery, while Reid praised the quarterback’s steady commitment.Those hours rarely came with the excitement of a packed stadium or the reward of a touchdown. Yet they were essential to giving Mahomes a chance to return without restrictions. Every session was an investment in the player he hoped to become again.Patrick Mahomes found motivation in the long road backRehabilitation can be a lonely process, especially for someone accustomed to leading a team. Mahomes had to measure progress in smaller victories: improved movement, greater strength and the ability to handle more work than the day before.He also had to resist the urge to compare his recovery with anyone else’s. Every injury is different, and rushing a return can put both a player and his team at risk.As Mahomes worked toward his comeback, the support around him helped him stay focused. The Chiefs’ medical staff, coaches and teammates remained part of a process that extended well beyond the field. Advice from other athletes who had faced major injuries also offered perspective on the patience required.The idea of competing through adversity has long been part of Mahomes’ career. But this challenge asked him to show that determination in a quieter way. There were no fourth-quarter drives to rescue, no defenders to evade and no immediate scoreboard to change.There was only the work in front of him.That kind of discipline can be difficult to appreciate from the outside. A successful comeback is often remembered as one triumphant moment, even though it rests on months of effort that few people see.Patrick Mahomes’ comeback brought him back to the fieldBy the time Mahomes returned to the field for the Chiefs’ 2026 season opener against Denver, the journey had stretched across months of uncertainty. His comeback was not simply about being cleared to play. It was about trusting the knee again, finding his rhythm and proving to himself that the long hours of rehabilitation had prepared him for the demands of NFL football.Mahomes delivered a memorable return on September 14, helping Kansas City defeat the Broncos 31-10. He threw two touchdown passes and added a rushing touchdown, giving Chiefs fans an early glimpse of what his return could mean for the team.The result did not erase the work that came before it. Instead, it gave that work a visible payoff. The quarterback who had spent much of the offseason rebuilding his knee was back competing, leading the offence and making plays.For Mahomes, the comeback also carried a larger lesson about motivation. As he put it in the context of his recovery, “That kind of keeps you motivated.”The road back was never guaranteed to unfold exactly as planned. But his return showed how sustained effort, patience and support can help an athlete move through a difficult stretch.Patrick Mahomes’ Super Bowl dream remains a powerful motivationMahomes’ return to the Chiefs gives him another opportunity to pursue the goal that has shaped so much of his career: winning another Super Bowl. The journey ahead will bring fresh challenges, and one strong performance cannot guarantee what the rest of the season will hold.Still, his recovery has already added a meaningful chapter to his NFL story. The injury forced him to step away from the game, but it also gave him a different test of leadership and resilience. He had to stay committed when the reward felt distant and progress came in small increments.That is what makes Mahomes’ comeback an inspiring story on sacrifice. The defining moments were not limited to his return against Denver. They began in the rehabilitation room, where he had to keep showing up, follow the plan and work toward a goal he could not reach overnight.Another Super Bowl remains an ambition, not a promise. But Mahomes has already demonstrated that his pursuit does not end when the path becomes difficult. His comeback was built one day at a time, and that steady commitment has brought him back to the field with another chance to chase football’s biggest prize.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jogo da NFL no Maracanã tem esquema especial de trânsito e segurança | G1
articles.standfirst: Partida entre Baltimore Ravens e Dallas Cowboys acontece no domingo (27) no Estádio do Maracanã, na Zona Norte do Rio.
articles.summary: A partida da NFL no Rio entre Ravens e Cowboys terá esquema especial de metrô e segurança com exigência de bolsas transparentes no Maracanã neste domingo.
articles.body:
Prefeitura do Rio anunciou esquema de trânsito para jogo da NFL no Maracanã — Foto: Divulgação/ Prefeitura do Rio

A Prefeitura do Rio divulgou, na manhã desta segunda-feira (21), o esquema especial de trânsito para a partida entre Baltimore Ravens e Dallas Cowboys, no Estádio do Maracanã, na Zona Norte da cidade. O confronto faz parte do NFL Rio Game 2026.

O jogo acontecerá no próximo domingo (27). A principal orientação das autoridades é que o público utilize transporte público para chegar ao estádio. Os portões serão abertos às 13h25.

A região do Maracanã terá restrições de estacionamento, com sinalização específica que será instalada ao longo da semana. Além das proibições de estacionamento já existentes, novas restrições entrarão em vigor das 19h até duas horas após o término da partida.

Segundo a presidente da CET-Rio , Marize da Silva Queiroz Ribeiro, o planejamento segue modelos adotados em grandes eventos realizados na cidade.

“Fizemos um planejamento semelhante ao que fizemos para a Copa, para as Olimpíadas e para a final da Libertadores, com uma grande intervenção na área”, afirmou a presidente da CET-Rio.

Durante a operação, o trânsito no sentido Méier será desviado pela Rua Ceará. Já os veículos que seguirem em direção à Tijuca deverão utilizar a Rua Mariz e Barros.

A CET-Rio recomenda o uso do metrô e dos trens urbanos para o deslocamento até o estádio. A orientação é que os pedestres sigam as instruções dos agentes de trânsito e de controle de fluxo.

O metrô funcionará das 7h às 23h. A estação indicada varia de acordo com o portão de acesso ao estádio:

Portões A e B: estação Maracanã/Rei Pelé (Linha 2);

Portão C: estação São Francisco Xavier/Tijuca (Linha 1);

Portões D e E: estação São Cristóvão (Linha 2).

A recomendação é que os torcedores utilizem o pagamento por aproximação diretamente nas catracas ou recarreguem antecipadamente o cartão Jaé.

Para evitar aglomerações, a orientação é chegar com antecedência e deixar o estádio de forma gradual após o fim da partida, seguindo as instruções dos fiscais.

Os espectadores de jogo da NFL no Rio de Janeiro podem acessar o estádio por diferentes estações de metrô — Foto: Divulgação/ Prefeitura do Rio

A Polícia Militar ficará responsável pela escolta das delegações e pela manutenção da ordem pública no entorno do evento, especialmente na região do Maracanã.

O policiamento será coordenado pelo Batalhão Especializado em Policiamento em Estádios (Bepe), com apoio do Batalhão Tático de Motociclistas (BTM). Outras unidades, como a Diretoria-Geral de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (DGTIC), o Batalhão de Policiamento em Áreas Turísticas (BPTur), o Grupamento de Policiamento Ferroviário (GPFer) e batalhões da área também participarão da operação.

“É um evento diferente de qualquer outro esporte para o qual prestamos segurança no Rio de Janeiro . Tem uma dinâmica específica e exigiu uma série de reuniões. Adaptamos nosso modelo ao padrão utilizado pela NFL em todo o mundo”, afirmou Victor Santos, secretário estadual de Segurança Pública.

A Polícia Civil também atuará com reforço de efetivo.

A organização informou que somente bolsas transparentes serão permitidas no estádio, medida que visa facilitar a inspeção do conteúdo pelos agentes de segurança.

“Haverá controle de acesso. É proibida a entrada com garrafas de vidro, objetos perfurocortantes, fogos de artifício e materiais incendiários, armas de fogo ou armas brancas, além de materiais de marketing não autorizados”, afirmou o secretário municipal de Ordem Pública, Marcus Belchior.
