articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 2: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels both injured on fluky plays
articles.summary: Chicago's Caleb Williams and Washington's Jayden Daniels, the first and second picks in the 2024 NFL Draft, were both injured Sunday.
articles.body:
You know it's a momentous week in the NFL when the Nos. 1 and 2 overall draft picks from the 2024 NFL Draft were carted off the field with injuries. Chicago 's Caleb Williams and Washington's Jayden Daniels both left their respective games after suffering injuries after failed red-zone plays with their teams trailing.

We'll have to wait to find out the severity of those injuries. But there were several other game-changing plays in Week 2 on Sunday, including ones from the Who Dat Heart Attacks, a tough moment for the league's oldest player and some weather-delayed heartbreak in Tampa .

The Bears scored 59 points in Week 1 and looked to have one of the NFL's best offenses. Everything changed in Week 2. The Vikings made life hard on Williams all game, and in the fourth quarter he suffered a hamstring injury on first-and-goal while attempting to scramble.

Tyson Bagent replaced Williams and couldn't get the Bears into the end zone the next two plays. Then the Vikings blocked the Bears' short field-goal try and drove down the field to take a 9-3 lead. Bagent had one more chance to be a hero in the final minute-plus but was sacked on the game's final play for a shocking Vikings victory .

This play couldn't have gone much worse for the Commanders. Trailing 17-10 in the closing seconds of the first half, Washington opted to go for it on third-and-goal from the Dallas 1-yard line instead of taking the field goal. Dropping back from center, QB Jayden Daniels was stepped on accidentally by center Nick Allegretti , and as Daniels fell back to the turf, he appeared to injure his left elbow.

Daniels was carted off after the teams had left the field for halftime, and the Commanders ruled him out before the start of the second half. The significance is that this is the same elbow Daniels injured last season — and later re-injured, which he described as "freak accidents." It appeared that Daniels suffered another one.

The New Orleans Saints couldn't finish off their Week 1 upset attempt, but they were successful doing so in Week 2. The Saints scored the final 15 points of the fourth quarter to turn a 17-9 deficit into a 24-17 victory at Baltimore . The key play was QB Tyler Shough's 1-yard sneak on fourth-and-goal with less than 90 seconds remaining, capping a 16-play drive. Ravens players argued Shough never got in, and the replay angles appeared inconclusive, so the score stood:

Shough led a wild comeback in Week 1, erasing a 21-0 deficit to the Lions on the road, but they fell in overtime when his throw to rookie Bryce Lance fell incomplete on a 2-point conversion attempt.

In Week 2, Shough led two 68-yard TD drives that ate up nearly 12 minutes of the fourth quarter, and the Saints intercepted Lamar Jackson in the waning moments to secure a statement victory on the road.

The Patriots didn't do a lot offensively, but they were in control of the game against the Steelers when Aaron Rodgers was strip-sacked by DT Christian Barmore . Elijah Ponder then scooped the loose ball and returned it 19 yards for a touchdown that put the game out of reach at 20-3.

Earlier in the game, the Patriots walloped Rodgers on another strip sack, which the Steelers recovered, resulting in a fourth-and-43 punt . Rodgers went 23-of-39 passing for 187 yards and an interception, taking four sacks. He was replaced by Mason Rudolph to close out the Patriots' 20-3 victory that raised questions about Rodgers and the Steelers' offense .

5. Browns' rain-delayed fourth-down stop

After a two-hour weather delay in Tampa, the Browns and Buccaneers got back to playing football. Prior to lightning and heavy rain blanketing the field, the Browns had taken a 23-19 lead and the Bucs were driving at the two-minute warning. Former Browns QB Baker Mayfield had Tampa Bay in business in the red zone, but he faced a fourth-and-11 do-or-die play to sting his ex-team. That's when this happened:

Mayfield just missed the throw, even if the Browns deserve credit for covering most of the play well. The Buccaneers had a timeout and needed only 11 yards for the first down, but Mayfield went for the kill shot — and it appeared he had Emeka Egbkua open.

The Bucs are 0-2, while the Browns improved to 1-1.

articles.title: Dallas' defense remains a real problem, limiting Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' potential
articles.summary: Were it not for Prescott, who's now 14-2 against Washington in his career, and CeeDee Lamb, who caught everything in a 200-mile radius, the trendy preseason...
articles.body:
Rarely does a single moment sum up an entire team's woes, but Dallas gave us one Sunday. With just eight seconds left in the first half, Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant was lying face-down and defenseless in his own end zone. Suddenly — and surely painfully — he took a cleat right to the butt courtesy of teammate Markquese Bell , who then stumbled awkwardly to the ground himself.

The only reason why that defenseless defense wasn't a perfect symbol of the Cowboys' hapless D in 2026 is that the opposing offense didn't score on the play.

Dallas beat perpetual rival Washington 37-20 on Sunday afternoon. CeeDee Lamb is already posting elite numbers. Dak Prescott notched yet another victory over an NFC East team. The Cowboys offense is humming along just fine.

But then there's the defense, whose entire strategy appears to be, "It's cool, Dak's gonna save us."

One week after Jaxson Dart diced up the Dallas secondary, Washington 's quarterbacks — Jayden Daniels in the first half, Marcus Mariota in the second — took their turn at the table. A win is a win, true, but you can't help but feel this game could have gone horribly wrong … which is a strange thing to say after a 17-point margin of victory.

Were it not for Prescott, who's now 14-2 against Washington in his career, and Lamb, who caught everything in a 200-mile radius, the trendy preseason Super Bowl pick would have started the season 0-2.

"I was worried about what it was going to be like if we did end up 0-2," team owner Jerry Jones conceded after the game. "And I can't say that I was a pillar of strength in my mentality coming into the game because I've got a lot of respect for the coaching over on the Washington Commander side. But having said all of that, this was a very important win for us."

But the Cowboys didn't fall to 0-2, so let's briefly focus on the positives here. Prescott, who finished 26-of-31 passing for 279 yards and four touchdowns, carved his name in Cowboys history, vaulting past Tony Romo for most passing touchdowns in franchise history at 249:

"Really great to see Dak break the record at home to CeeDee," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game. "I just thought the passing game was hitting on all cylinders today."

Lamb had 89 yards receiving in the first quarter, finishing with eight receptions on nine targets for 153 yards and a pair of touchdowns on the day. Tight end Jake Ferguson snagged another two touchdowns himself, and the Dallas offense remains both cinematic and productive.

The defense? Yeah, not so much. For the second straight game, this group committed boneheaded penalties that wiped out sacks or kept drives alive, allowed rushers to grind out extra yardage and receivers to get loose, and generally looked overwhelmed and overmatched in virtually every phase of the game.

Fate cut the Cowboys a break when Daniels stumbled on the final play of the first half and dislocated his left elbow, an injury that forced him out of the rest of the game . And yet Dallas allowed Mariota, still slinging it in the year 2026, to craft two second-half scoring drives and very nearly tie a game that the Cowboys had controlled throughout.

Washington had its opportunities. On at least two separate occasions, Washington passers couldn't connect with wide-open receivers who'd gotten past the Dallas secondary and into the end zone. Officials also deemed a third-quarter should-have-been-a-TD an incomplete pass, and Washington had to settle for a field goal rather than potentially tying the game at 17:

The defense also struggled with the little things like containing Washington on crucial third-and-long situations, so much so that by the end of the first half, Prescott was whirling a towel on the sideline trying to rally his defense. (It didn't work; Washington converted, although the half ran out soon afterward.)

This all accrues to new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who's now posted a second straight dog of a game. Dallas can't afford many more of these. "We don't feel like we have a finished product," Schottenheimer said , underselling the problem by galactic margins.

Hope isn't a strategy, and nor is hoping your prolific offense will score enough to outrun your woeful defense every week. Struggling to defend both the pass and run, struggling to contain both pocket passers and mobile ones … these aren't the building blocks of a sound organization.

If the Cowboys aren't able to figure out how to stop weak offenses and slow down better ones, it won't just be the defense getting its butt stomped this season … it'll be the whole team.

articles.title: Ben Johnson's offense teased transcendence. It then lost Caleb Williams and slipped vs. Brian Flores' Vikings
articles.summary: The Bears have more problems on their paws than just the status of their franchise quarterback.
articles.body:
CHICAGO — Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III stared out into open space, motionless as if he was a mannequin. Offensive tackle Theo Benedet mirrored that position.

There was deafening silence in the locker room as reporters filtered in from the bowels of a soggy Soldier Field, where the Bears dropped their home and NFC North opener Sunday to the Minnesota Vikings 9-3 and, more notably, lost their tantalizing quarterback, Caleb Wiliams, to a scary hamstring injury .

Murmurs of questions began to push against the stillness that enveloped the room. Five-time All-Pro left guard Joe Thuney , a 6-foot-5, 301-pound giant who was named NFL Protector of the Year in 2025, kept gently and somewhat helplessly returning to the same refrain.

"I hope Caleb's OK," he repeated to Yahoo Sports.

Hope is all the Bears can do after their on-field maestro stumbled and then tumbled while awkwardly sliding to a stop well short of a potential go-ahead touchdown midway through the fourth quarter of a divisional slugfest.

Amid unrelenting rain, wind and defensive schematics, Williams — the face of this year's Madden and the heart of the burgeoning Bears — rolled around in agony. The Fox broadcast picked up his haunting screams.

"Eighteen get hurt, I'm worried," rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad II said, referencing Williams' jersey number. "Everybody in the whole stadium was worried, maybe the whole world."

A week after orchestrating a 59-point, season-opening fantasia on the road against the Carolina Panthers , the 24-year-old found himself in the medical tent and eventually on a cart to the tunnel, with his offense stuck at three points. Before fans could even process the injury, Minnesota added insult to it, blocking what would have been a game-tying Chicago field goal. The Vikings tacked on another of their own before denying Bears backup Tyson Bagent a heroic comeback, fittingly finishing the rock fight with their fourth and final sack on a day vaunted defensive coordinator Brian Flores called for blitzes close to 80% of the time .

Quarterbacked Sunday by a 33-year-old Carson Wentz , Minnesota quietly won its seventh game in a row, a streak that dates back to last season. The Vikings are used to playing a game of musical chairs at the sport's most important position. Williams brought Chicago a temporary reprieve in that exercise. He started all 17 games his rookie year after the franchise tapped him with the No. 1 overall draft pick in 2024. The former Heisman Trophy winner ran that workload back again last season, in addition to starring in two playoff games.

Now it's all but certain he'll be sidelined. Head coach Ben Johnson told reporters postgame that the Bears won't know the severity of Williams' hamstring issue until Monday, exactly one week prior to hosting the 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles for "Monday Night Football."

"I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee," Johnson said. "That was my first inclination. But yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. So we'll see how bad it is tomorrow, and we'll go from there."

Despite the despondence in the locker room, there seems to be confidence among the team that Williams could be back sooner than later.

Johnson noted that Williams was "in good spirits." Muhammad recalled a conversation he had with Williams in the aftermath of the defeat and assured the media, "He going to be good." A similar tenor was presented by others, namely wideout Rome Odunze .

Injuries are part of football, and Williams is resilient. A variation of that anthem permeated.

"He Superman, he do his thing, but he is human, and sometimes in this game, it's unpredictable," Bears defensive lineman Grady Jarrett said of Williams.

'Against a good defense like that, you just can't shoot yourself in the foot'

The Bears have more problems on their paws than just the status of their franchise quarterback.

In the first half at Carolina last week, Chicago amassed 31 points and 315 yards. This time around, the Bears accrued their measly three points and just 93 yards over the opening two quarters of competition. It was a 180, and, as Johnson emphasized, "the weather was a major factor," but there was a common thread among those polar performances.

The Bears were flagged nine times in the first half against the Panthers. They racked up seven penalties in the first half versus the Vikings. That blemish most prominently reared its head late in the second quarter.

A 14-yard pass to tight end Colston Loveland would have vaulted Chicago to the Minnesota 16-yard line had an illegal shift not wiped that gain off the board. Next came a holding penalty, then an intentional grounding infraction. The unwanted whistles resumed directly after running back D'Andre Swift picked up 11 yards on a reception. A false start marked the fourth penalty in five snaps for a Bears offense that Johnson wants to score more points than anyone ever .

Suddenly, Chicago stared down the barrel of a second-and-35 from its own 45-yard line.

"Last week, we had some penalties as well, but I feel like we capitalized when we had opportunities for looks," Bears right tackle Darnell Wright told Yahoo Sports.

"This week we didn't do as good a job. Obviously with the elements, blah, blah, blah, whatever, but I mean they're playing in the elements, too. That's just the biggest thing, just cashing in on our opportunities when they present [themselves] — don't shoot ourselves in the foot."

Johnson said more of the same at the podium: "Against a good defense like that, you just can't shoot yourself in the foot. We had way too many turnovers, the blocked field goal hurts and then we had missed red-zone opportunities just as a whole."

The Bears missed out on a game-winning touchdown from the Minnesota 12-yard line in Bagent's spot duty. However, their more significant error took place right out of the break. Following halftime, Chicago finally generated offensive momentum, only for Swift to fumble the rock a yard shy of the end zone.

A feather in Flores' cap and a Bears backup plan

Nearly all the chatter consuming the lead-up to Sunday's showdown centered on Johnson and Flores, a pair of football scientists who tinker with Xs and Os like they're carefully handling beakers in a lab. They combine deception and aggression to concoct a conceptual mixture that vexes opponents, including one another.

Before this iteration of their budding rivalry, Johnson came out on top of five of their previous six matchups, a stretch that began in 2023 when Johnson was becoming a household name as the Detroit Lions ' offensive coordinator.

Granted Flores had Mother Nature on his side Sunday, but he won the latest round of the proverbial boxing match.

"There's some things that, looking back at it, I'd love to do a little bit differently," Johnson said. "And that's what makes it so challenging to go against this guy. I think he did a great job.

"We get a little momentum coming out of halftime there, and we make it all the way down, and then we kind of give it up."

He added: "We had some points in the bag, I thought."

Although Williams was tied for sixth last season in EPA per dropback against the blitz, per NGS , he wasn't blitzed by Flores as much as he was Sunday. The Vikings' rushers stifled Williams, especially linebackers Dallas Turner (two sacks) and Andrew Van Ginkel (one sack). Building on his head-turning Week 1, Turner flushed Williams out of the pocket down the stretch of the first quarter, leading to an errant throw that cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. intercepted.

The Bears are going back to the drawing board — and likely handing Bagent the chalk.

Defensive back Cam Lewis told Yahoo Sports that, if that's the case, the team's "still in good hands." Wide receiver Kalif Raymond described Bagent as "a guy who puts in the work."

"He was ready for the moment," Raymond continued, referencing the former Division II standout and one-time undrafted free agent. "He's always going to be ready for the moment. You can tell by the way he works in practice."

That praise hung in the air and battled the hush that pervaded the locker room minutes earlier when reporters first showed up.

articles.title: Browns HC Todd Monken claps back at Mike Tomlin barb after win over Bucs: 'Browns are gonna Browns — f*** that'
articles.summary: Monken said that Cleveland players took criticism of their Week 1 play to heart before a 23-19 away win over the Bucs.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken says that the team won't let years of struggles bog down their current season, no matter what other people say.

In a news conference after the Browns held on for a 23-19 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Monken got fired up when speaking about the team's week-to-week improvement. The coach then concluded his time with reporters with an apparent reference to something that NBC analyst Mike Tomlin said on air earlier this week.

The Browns started their season with a dismal loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , prompting Tomlin to give a blunt assessment of the game. The former longtime Pittsburgh Steelers coach-turned-analyst evoked one of his former players while speaking about Cleveland's loss on "Football Night in America": "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster , 'the Browns is the Browns,'" Tomlin said.

After Sunday's win, Monken said that the Week 1 struggles fueled their victory and brought the team closer.

"I thought our guys did a great job of hanging together. We had a couple scuffles Wednesday, which is good. That's awesome. 'Cause guys didn't like it, right? They're a little pissed off. You oughta be a little pissed off. (We) played awful. It wasn't the standard," Monken said.

That's Monken ended his news conference on a mic drop — with a bit of explicit language.

"Browns are gonna Browns. F*** that!" Monken said. "The guys took that to heart."

Monken's response on Sunday was much fierier than his initial reaction to Tomlin's comments: On Monday, Monken seemed frustrated at the assessment when asked about it in a news conference .

"Everybody's afforded their opinions. That's what you do when you go from coaching to television," Monken said. "I don't see it that way, 'Browns being Browns.' I don't see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn't play well. That's one week. That's not 'Browns being Browns,' that's Browns being poorly on one week … The only way to change people's opinions is to play better. That's a fact."

With Monken pushing back on Tomlin, the former Steelers coach laughed off his former NFL opponent's words on the Indianapolis Colts-Kansas City Chiefs Sunday Night Football broadcast.

"Hey, I'm glad that I can still motivate, although I'm not coaching anymore," Tomlin joked.

Tomlin added more during halftime , saying that he has "respect" for the Browns playing with "spirit" on Sunday.

"I love my role, that's what I have to say for myself. You know why? Because I can provide bulletin board material with no personal consequence," Tomlin said with a laugh. "You gotta give them credit for what transpired this week, particularly on their defense … Cleveland's defense showed up today.

Sunday's win was broken up by a two-hour weather delay after lightning and heavy rains came through Tampa . The stoppage started right at the two-minute warning in the second half, with the Buccaneers retaining the ball when they returned. However, the Browns defense came up big to stop Tampa Bay from scoring a potentially game-winning touchdown in the final seconds.

A lot of criticism in Cleveland focused on Monken's choice to start Deshaun Watson at quarterback again despite Watson's on- and off-field issues. Watson had a solid game on Sunday, throwing for 238 yards and two touchdowns.

Cleveland was down by as many as 10 points, but scored 17 points in the second half to pull ahead. Monken noted in Sunday's news conference that he was "so proud" of the team for battling back for the win.

"We didn't put our best foot forward last week," Monken said. "We played a lot cleaner this week. Not perfect. But I'm gonna enjoy this win for our guys."

articles.title: Chargers flop again as Jim Harbaugh falls to 0-2 for first time as a head coach while surprising Raiders improve to 2-0
articles.summary: Jim Harbaugh is 0-2 as a head coach for the first time. In the NFL or college.
articles.body:
The Chargers dropped to 0-2 on Sunday, falling to the Raiders 26-14 in yet another putrid offensive performance at home.

Justin Herbert had another rough game, being picked twice, and the Chargers fumbled six times, their most in a game since 1987. They lost only one of them, but it was a killer: Omarion Hampton coughed it up in Las Vegas territory with the Chargers trailing 17-14 with less than four minutes remaining.

The Raiders capitalized, with Kirk Cousins hitting Cody White — who entered Sunday with one career touchdown — on his second TD of the game. Cousins threw for three scores, and Tre Tucker finished with a game-high 119 receiving yards and a score.

New head coach Klint Kubiak has led the Raiders to their first 2-0 start since 2021, which is coincidentally the last time the franchise made the playoffs. Bill Callahan in 2002 was the last first-year Raiders coach to start 2-0.

Jim Harbaugh has never started a season 0-2 as a head coach — in the NFL or college football. Oh, and the Chargers' schedule suddenly gets very thorny , with three of the next four on the road and some heavyweight opponents awaiting.

His quarterback is struggling. Even star left tackle Joe Alt had a nightmare game going up against Maxx Crosby , who helped coax Alt into four penalties — including a hold resulting in a safety in the final few minutes while the Chargers still nominally had a chance to come back.

The Chargers, who flopped badly in a Week 1 home loss to the Cardinals, opened the game with a missed field goal, two quick punts and an interception. The Raiders didn't exactly set the world on fire offensively, but they did strike first with Cousins hitting Tucker on a 40-yard TD.

The Chargers tied it on Hampton's 1-yard TD run, but the Raiders took a 10-7 edge into halftime after Matt Gay 's 59-yard field goal.

After the Chargers' defense held the Raiders to a three-and-out on the opening drive of the third quarter, Justin Herbert led a strong touchdown drive to give the Chargers a 14-10 lead.

It didn't last long. The Raiders matched them with their own 74-yard scoring drive, with Cousins hitting White — primarily a special teamer — on just his second career TD reception, giving them a 17-14 lead. Not a bad grab for a guy with 11 receptions entering Sunday.

The Raiders gave the Chargers a chance when they came out of a defensive timeout with 12 men on the field for Los Angeles ' fourth-and-1 play, keeping the drive alive. That's when Hampton coughed up the fumble that Jeremy Chinn ran back 43 yards.

The Raiders' unexpectedly strong start has given their season a new perspective. The Chargers now have to find a way to pick up the pieces after a disastrous 0-2 start, losing to two teams who were near the bottom of the standings a year ago.

articles.title: A 33-30 nail-biter that exposed every Chiefs weakness, yet somehow ended with Kansas City sitting at 2-0
articles.summary: NFL News: Kansas City needed overtime, a fumble reversal, and Harrison Butker's right foot to put away an Indianapolis Colts team that had no business keeping t.
articles.body: Kansas City needed overtime, a fumble reversal, and Harrison Butker's right foot to put away an Indianapolis Colts team that had no business keeping this game alive as long as it did. Patrick Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns Sunday night at Arrowhead. Kenneth Walker III rushed for 117 yards. Travis Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards. The Chiefs won 33-30. And yet, for long stretches, it felt like the whole thing could fall apart at any moment.How did the Chiefs almost lose to an 0-2 Colts team?The short answer is that Indianapolis Colts played with genuine fight. Daniel Jones was not spectacular, but he was enough. He finished with 210 yards, a touchdown, and one interception. Jonathan Taylor did damage too, carrying the ball for 92 yards and two scores. The Colts moved the ball, ran the clock, and stayed in a game most people had written off before kickoff.What really put Kansas City on the edge was what happened in overtime. Butker hit a 31-yard field goal to give the Chiefs the lead, and for a second, Arrowhead exhaled. Then Laquon Treadwell caught a deep ball from Jones, the ball came loose, the Chiefs recovered, and Arrowhead exhaled again. Except the replay officials stepped in and overturned it. Down by contact. Colts' ball. Spencer Shrader hit a 38-yarder to tie it back up, and suddenly the whole stadium was nervous again.Kansas City's defense gave up chunks of yardage all night. Their secondary got beaten repeatedly. The offense had its moments but also had long spells where Mahomes was doing more than he should have to hold things together. For a team with championship aspirations, that is a concern worth noting, even if the final result says otherwise.Why did the Chiefs win despite looking vulnerable for most of the game?Because of Walker, and because of Butker, and honestly because the Colts made one key mistake too many. After the overtime reset, Kansas City got the ball back with 3:11 left. Walker took three straight handoffs to move the chains past midfield. Then Mahomes hit him on a 22-yard pass, and just like that, Butker was back out there for a 40-yarder. It went through. Game over.That drive said something real about this team. When they had to grind it out, they did. No deep throws, no risks. Just Walker carrying the rock and Mahomes finding him in the flat when the moment called for it. It was not pretty. But playoff football rarely is.The Chiefs are 2-0. They have gaps in this roster that Sunday night made visible. But they also have the one thing that covers a lot of flaws: they know how to finish.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Weekend Review: Brian Flores dominates Chicago Bears, Tyler Shough heroics and more Justin Herbert misery
articles.summary: The NFL Weekend Review guides you through the best of the action from across the league on the road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles; watch the New York Giants against the Los Angeles Rams in Monday Night Football from 1.15am Tuesday, live on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears scored 59 points in Week One of the NFL season. On Sunday, they scored three. Welcome to the Brian Flores experience.

It had been billed as the ultimate chess match between two of modern football's smartest and most unhinged minds, Ben Johnson's free-scoring offense against Flores' blitz-heavy Minnesota Vikings defense. Their collision of controlled chaos would lean in favour of the latter as the Vikings claimed a 9-3 victory, coming with the minor asterisk of Bears quarterback Caleb Williams leaving the game due to a hamstring injury midway through the fourth quarter.

Williams was blitzed on 81.8 per cent of his drop backs prior to his departure, according to NextGen Stats. It made for a blitz rate that would have ranked as the third highest in a game since at least 2018.

By the end of the game the Vikings had recorded four sacks, 10 quarterback hits and seven pass breakups, capped by Dallas Turner's game-icing sack of Tyson Bagent on the final play. With the win Flores improved to 2-1 in his duels with Johnson since the latter's appointment as Bears head coach, and 5-2 dating back to Johnson's time as Detroit Lions offensive coordinator.

It was the latest marquee addition to a brimming resume in the campaign to launch Flores back into head coaching contention. In fact, that he isn't already an NFL head coach again is an injustice. Few in the league are capable of stifling a Johnson offense with such command, guile and fire-with-fire aggression, Flores further bolstering what has become a glowing reputation during his time alongside Kevin O'Connell in Minnesota.

The narrative in Minnesota has long been O'Connell's ability to achieve a lot with little when it comes to accentuating and elevating once-written-off quarterbacks. But Flores' influence has been equal if not superior when it comes to keeping the Vikings in playoff relevance. From the variation and ludicrousy of his blitz angles, to the way he manipulates the versatility of multi-faceted personnel like Josh Metellus, Flores has forged one of the most dynamic units in football.

It helps, too, to unlock a star pass rusher, and it appears Flores is the perfect man to raise the curtain on Dallas Turner's breakout campaign. Turner added two sacks to his tally, including the finisher on the final play, while notching 10 more pressures to lift his total to a league-high 20 through two weeks.

The Vikings defense is among the best in the league, and Flores is the primary reason. The Bears, Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions are praying the silver lining to this is that he won't be around in the NFC North much longer. If football is being honest with itself, he should be a head coach in the next cycle. He probably should be already.

Long live the box office Brian Flores blitz.

Jaylen Waddle has arrived in Denver. The Broncos wide receiver announced himself on his home opener in Mile High with eight catches for 138 yards as Denver overcame a slow start to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 in a response to their Week One loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and a bounce back game of sorts for new play-caller Davis Webb. Waddle highlighted his value to the Broncos offense in the second quarter when he flipped the field with a 49 reception in tight coverage to set his side up at the one, sparking his offense into life in the process. He is the splash play outlet Bo Nix needed to take this aerial attack forward.

The New Orleans have a quarterback. For the second week in a row Tyler Shough spearheaded a Saints comeback, this one though ending in victory as Kellen Moore's side stunned Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens in a 24-17 win. The Saints entered the fourth quarter trailing 17-9 before Shough went 12 of 14 passing for 119 yards, one touchdown pass and one rushing touchdown to cap the fightback. It came a week after Shough shrugged off his poor start to throw for 410 yards and three touchdowns as the Saints fell 31-30 to the Detroit Lions in an overtime thriller, both performances underlining his blossoming connection to Chris Olave. The former Ohio State Buckeye had eight catches for 86 yards and a touchdown on Sunday as he seeks to establish himself among the premium wide receivers in football.

Kevin Stefanski is in hell. Once at the helm of a quarterback nightmare in Cleveland, he is now staring at a similar state of sputtering purgatory in Atlanta, where his Falcons just fell to 0-2 after a 34-3 defeat to the Panthers. With Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr out, Cooper Rush took the reins again under center as he completed just 10 of 17 passes for 86 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions, before fourth string option Jack Strand went eight of 15 for 59 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception. It makes defending Bijan Robinson that little bit easier when opponents know every down is reliant on him, the Falcons running back still mustering 72 yards from 16 carries as one of the most unjustly wasted stars in football.

Justin Herbert may need to move on from the Los Angeles Chargers in order to reignite his NFL career. There will always be the argument it would and should have happened for him by now were he worthy of recognition among the league's elite quarterbacks, but between a talent vacuum on offense in recent years and a sack tally higher than any other quarterback since he entered the league, there is an undeniable flip side to his struggles. After falling to the Arizona Cardinals in Week One, he was dealt another low on Sunday as the Chargers lost 26-14 to Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders. Herbert finished the game 15 of 27 for 192 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions while being sacked three times. This was supposed to be the season of fireworks alongside new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel; so far, it has been a disaster with no sign of prospective Chargers contention. The lack of playoff win is an overbearing monkey on his back, and now the pressure is truly mounting. Herbert isn't playing well and isn't immune to criticism, and this has become a bizarre situation in Los Angeles.

Ja'Marr Chase : Joe Burrow's star weapon delivered another reminder of why he stakes a claim for being the best receiver in football with an absurd swivelling, back-peddling 32-yard touchdown catch in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over the Houston Texans. He finished the game with seven catches for 75 yards and two scores as Zac Taylor's leading stars neutralised one of the most feared defenses in the league.

DeVonta Smith: With AJ Brown no longer in the fold, DeVonta Smith is the unequivocal No 1 in Philadelphia. On Sunday, he lived up to the task with an instrumental role in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Tennessee Titans. Trailing by three and staring at third-and-six in the final 20 seconds, Jalen Hurts floated deep in the direction of Smith, who was on hand to make a leaping grab that would set-up Darius Cooper's game-winning three-yard touchdown catch. It featured within a defining performance that saw Smith make 10 receptions for 117 yards and a score.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba: The reigning Offensive Player of the Year continues to reach new heights, recording one of the best games of his Super Bowl-winning NFL career with nine catches for 155 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals, who in comparison had just 151 yards in total as a team.

Jesse Minter: Wavering identity tripped up Jesse Minter and his Ravens on Sunday as they threw away a fourth-quarter lead in a 24-17 loss to the Saints. They had looked in command behind Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry early, the latter of whom ran in a touchdown out of wildcat formation. Declan Doyle's offense then saw Henry carry the ball just five times for 17 yards in the second half, drifting from their star running back to pave the way for the Saints fight-back.

Baker Mayfield: Revenge game defeats are tough. Revenge game defeats to the Cleveland Browns taste that little bit more bitter. Being out-played by Deshaun Watson in a revenge game defeat tastes even worse. That's what happened on Sunday as Mayfield's Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to a 23-19 defeat to Browns, the newly-paid quarterback failing to find Emeka Egbuka for a game-winning touchdown pass in the final 20 seconds.

Player of the Weekend - Devin Lloyd, LB, Carolina Panthers

Devin Lloyd was unfortunate not to get his bumper pay-day in Jacksonville this past year, but is already looking like one of the best free agency signings of the offseason. The linebacker, who signed a three-year $45m deal with the Carolina Panthers, starred with two interceptions, one pick-six, one sack, three pass breakups, nine tackles and two tackles for loss in his side's 34-3 victory over the Atlanta Falcons.

Let's go with Denver's home win over the Jaguars, mainly because I was here and on hand to experience the Mile High atmosphere for the first time in my career. What I did enjoy was the eruption of boos from the home fans as the big-screen displayed the number of 'no shows' for the game, which is apparently a regular feature here. The noise is quite incredible, even from inside what is sold as a sound-proof press box. Multiple penalties and a sluggish start prompted some early groans from Denver locals, but by the end their elite defense had resumed its league-leading work of last season to thwart Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen's Jags offense. Bo Nix, too, has found a new best friend in Waddle, making for a passing attack capable of stretching the field.

Jayden Daniels was handed a fresh injury setback as he dislocated his left elbow again less than a year after the injury that saw him sidelined for the second half of last season.

Daniels was taken off on a cart at the end of the first half of Washington's 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams also suffered a right hamstring injury that saw him exit midway through the fourth quarter of Chicago's defeat to the Vikings.

"We'll know more tomorrow [Monday]," said Bears head coach Ben Johnson.

"I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee. That was my first inclination, but the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. We'll see how bad it is tomorrow, and we'll go from there."

articles.title: NFL Results Week Two: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels injured as Patrick Mahomes shines for Chiefs
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs look back to their best but Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels suffer serious injuries. Here's what you need to know from week two in the NFL.
articles.body:
After a feast of points in week one, defences hit back in week two of the NFL.

The Chicago Bears came crashing back down to earth after a flying start - and they suffered one of the two worrying injuries to two of the league's top young quarterbacks.

The Kansas City Chiefs were back doing what they do best but the Baltimore Ravens were surprisingly beaten, while two games were settled in overtime and one decided with just nine seconds on the clock.

Here's our pick from Sunday's week two action.

Allen stars as Bills open new stadium in style

Superstar quarterbacks suffer serious injuries

The Chicago Bears scored 59 points last week but just three this time in an ugly 9-3 home loss to the Vikings, as Minnesota won their seventh straight game at Soldier Field.

The 56-point drop-off is the second most in NFL history as the Bears saw two touchdowns lost with a dropped catch and a fumble, had a field goal blocked but worst of all lost their star quarterback Caleb Williams.

The first pick of the 2024 draft was carried off the field in the fourth quarter looking in serious pain, but initial reports are that his hamstring injury may not be as serious as first feared.

Jayden Daniels was the second pick of that 2024 draft behind Williams and he left Washington's defeat at Dallas with a serious injury to the same elbow he dislocated last season.

Daniels, who seems certain to be out for some time, would still have struggled to keep up with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott who threw four touchdowns in their 37-20 victory.

Prescott surpassed Tony Romo's team record of 248 touchdown passes by taking his tally to 249.

Classic Kansas City Chiefs win in overtime

The Kansas City Chiefs gave another ominous sign that they were back in business with a 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Winning tight games was a hallmark of the Patrick Mahomes dynasty during three recent Super Bowl wins, so there was a familiar feeling when Harrison Butker kicked the winning field goal right at the death.

Mahomes threw three touchdowns and his 382 passing yards was his most for three years. Travis Kelce had 101 yards and a touchdown and summer signing Kenneth Walker had another huge game.

The Super Bowl MVP had 178 total yards and was crucial in overtime to help overcome a strong challenge from Daniel Jones and the Colts - who may have lost their first two games but look to have plenty to build on.

The Green Bay Packers also triumphed in overtime by erasing a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter against the New York Jets to win 20-17 - and snap a six-game losing streak.

Super Bowl champions Seattle look the real deal again after beating the Arizona Cardinals 31-7 for a 12th straight win.

Drew Lock showed he is no ordinary back-up quarterback with three touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, including an 82 yarder that is the longest of the talented receiver's career.

The Seahawks lost Walker to the Chiefs but have retained a remarkable 17 of 22 starters and 44 of their 53-man roster from last season's title win.

That consistency should see them go close again, but they'll face a rejuvenated San Francisco 49ers in their division, who are also 2-0 after beating the Miami Dolphins 35-15.

Showing no signs of jet leg from their victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, the Niners scored touchdowns on their first five possessions to blow Miami away - Christian McCaffrey scored twice, George Kittle also found the end zone and Brock Purdy accounted for three scores.

With the 49ers having their defensive stars back from injury Kyle Shanahan's squad look the total package once again.

The Cincinnati Bengals also look more well rounded this season after winning a 20-6 battle in Houston, thanks to an early touchdown of the season contender catch from Ja'Marr Chase.

We expect fireworks from Chase and Joe Burrow, but having a defence capable of keeping CJ Stroud out of the end zone, and sacking him four times in a road game is the biggest reason for optimism among Bengals fans.

The Philadelphia Eagles were on the ropes against the Tennessee Titans until Jalen Hurts threw the winning touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with just nine seconds left in the game.

Although not as impressive overall as other 2-0 sides, that ability to win games at the death is a familiar trait with Philly - and will make them dangerous all season again.

The New Orleans Saints just fell short after a monster comeback in Detroit last week, but went one better this week by upsetting Lamar Jackson's Baltimore Ravens 24-17 in their home opener.

Tyler Shough bundled over in a big crowd for a slightly controversial touchdown given the ball was largely unsighted, before two-time MVP Jackson then threw a late interception when trying to salvage the game.

The Saints may just surprise a few more teams this season.

Surprising everyone right now are the Las Vegas Raiders, who sit on 2-0 after winning 26-14 at the hapless Chargers.

The Chargers have lost by double digits to two of last season's biggest strugglers and with away games at Buffalo and Seattle, things look likely to get much worse.

DeShaun Watson threw a fourth quarter touchdown as the Cleveland Browns also sprung an upset win on the road in Tampa Bay, with a weather delay meaning they had to wait an extra two hours to seal the deal.

Perhaps the biggest surprise so far though is just how bad the Atlanta Falcons are. They were beaten 34-3 by the Carolina Panthers to become just the fourth team since 1978 to fail to get into an opponents red zone in their first two games.

The quarterback mess has played a part - and what summed them up nicely was undrafted rookie Jack Strand replacing a struggling Cooper Rush, and duly threw a pick six.

Atlanta could already be eyeing the first draft pick next year if this continues.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Addresses Refs' Controversial Fumble Call, 'Didn't Want to See Twitter's Reaction'
articles.summary: Having come out on the winning end, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes could laugh about the controversial non-fumble in overtime of Sunday's 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Having come out on the winning end, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes could laugh about the controversial non-fumble in overtime of Sunday's 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.

"I was actually kind of glad," he told reporters (1:07 mark). "I didn't want to see Twitter's reaction if they gave us the ball."

Colts receiver Laquon Treadwell hauled in a long pass to put Indy in the red zone and then lost possession. Following a review, officials ruled him down by contact before the fumble.

The call didn't decide the game. The Colts had to settle for a 38-yard field goal by Spencer Shrader, and Harrison Butker won it for Kansas City with a 40-yarder.

"In Spags we trust," tight end Travis Kelce said to ESPN's Scott Van Pelt, referring to defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo (5:30 mark). "In that defense we trust. We trust those guys to give us a chance, and sure enough, they had a huge red-zone stand. Force them to get a field goal and get the ball back in Pat Mahomes' hands. We knew as an offense if we got the opportunity to close that thing out, we were gonna do it."

Any team that's consistently good over a period of years is inevitably accused of getting a favorable whistle, and the Chiefs are no different. A segment of NFL fans are convinced the refs have a bias toward Kansas City regardless of whether there's any firm evidence to support that theory.

If anything, Sunday night showed the opposite. Maybe it was the correct call, but close scrutiny of the play wasn't definitive. Ruling that Treadwell fumbled the ball probably wouldn't have caused an uproar.

Mahomes may have had a different opinion on the situation if the Colts went on to find the end zone later in the possession.

Following Cleveland's weather-delayed 23-19 comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium, Monken walked toward the field-level railing and exchanged high-fives with members of the traveling Dawg Pound.

The Browns shared the heartwarming moment on their official social channels. It captured Monken's appreciation for supporters who remained through torrential rain and an approximately two-hour lightning delay. Their presence provided a fitting backdrop to a gritty victory. Cleveland's defense ultimately held Tampa Bay out of the end zone during a decisive late red-zone stand. For Monken, the scene reflected the resilient identity he has sought to establish since taking charge of the franchise.

Monken has built an NFL career around aggressive offensive design and maximizing his personnel. He entered the league as Jacksonville 's wide receivers coach in 2007 before becoming Tampa Bay's offensive coordinator from 2016–18. That's when the Buccaneers led the NFL in passing yards during that span. After a 2019 season as Cleveland's offensive coordinator, Monken returned to college football and helped Georgia produce back-to-back national championship-winning offenses. He returned to the NFL in 2023 as Baltimore 's offensive coordinator. Monken helped Lamar Jackson win MVP while the Ravens led the league in rushing and yards per play. Cleveland hired Monken as its 19th full-time head coach in January 2026. They brought him back to the franchise with the task of building a new era. At 1–1, his first victory now has an image to match the message: Cleveland fights, and the Dawg Pound stays with it.

It's still early into the 2026 NFL season, but the Los Angeles Chargers couldn't have gotten off to a worse start.

Los Angeles lost 26-14 to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday to fall to 0-2. Opta pointed out it achieved something that hasn't happened in a century. It's rarely an encouraging sign when you're in the same company as a franchise (Racine Tornadoes) nobody has heard of:

More than just the outcome itself, the manner of the defeat was discouraging for the Chargers. Star quarterback Justin Herbert went 15-of-27 for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, and the defense allowed the Raiders to average 5.1 yards per play.

It's reductive to put this all on Herbert's shoulders. Sure, this isn't what fans envisioned early into two-time Pro Bowler's partnership with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, but the personnel issues go beyond the quarterback position.

Given what Los Angeles' schedule looks like moving forward, the team could sink even further. Here are the next seven opponents: Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens.

How many of those games are you confident about the Chargers winning? They could be a long shot for the playoffs by the time they head into their Week 7 bye.

Look at the bright side. They're bound to at least exist through to November, which is something the Tornadoes couldn't say in 1926.

Sometimes you have to find the small victories.

articles.title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott Eyes Lofty TD Goal After Breaking Tony Romo's Franchise Record
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott doesn't intend to slow down after setting a franchise record in Sunday's 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott doesn't intend to slow down after setting a franchise record in Sunday's 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders.

Prescott notched the 249th touchdown pass of his NFL career, putting him above Tony Romo in the Cowboys' record book. He told reporters after the game he was "blessed, honored" to achieve the feat.

"As I told you earlier in the week, records are meant to be broken," he said. "This is my time to break this one. Pretty cool to do it against the team I threw my first touchdown against 10 years ago or so. Definitely humbling, something I don't take for granted. The great history of this organization, of the past quarterbacks before me…

"Super, super honored. Super thankful. God's great. Not taking it lightly. But as I told you, it's just the beginning. I want to double it and plan to play for a while, so just getting started."

Prescott dissected the Commanders secondary to the tune of 279 yards and four touchdowns through the air.

Doubling his touchdown total won't put the four-time Pro Bowler at the top of the NFL's all-time list, but he would enter impressive company. Tom Brady holds the record with 649 touchdown passes, and only four other quarterbacks have 500 or more.

Prescott's goal is pretty ambitious given his age (33) and the fact he's into his 11th season. He'll need to remain healthy and productive for a long time to approach 500 TDs.

articles.title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott Jokes About 2012 Tony Romo Post After Breaking Record, 'I Was Just a Dumb Fan'
articles.summary: After breaking Tony Romo's franchise record for the most touchdown passes in Dallas Cowboys history in Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders, star quarterback Dak Prescott reflected on his infamous 2012 tweet about his predecessor.
articles.body:
After breaking Tony Romo's franchise record for the most touchdown passes in Dallas Cowboys history in Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders, star quarterback Dak Prescott reflected on his infamous 2012 tweet about his predecessor.

After Romo threw three interceptions in that 28-18 loss to Washington, Prescott tweeted, "I'm DONE taking up for Romo," adding the hashtag "#hadenough." He followed up with more tweets saying that Romo "doesn't finish and none of those interceptions are on the offensive line. #noexcuses," and "You're supposed to throw it over the guy's head. That was the most embarrassing one of them all. #stoptakingupforhim."

Prescott threw four touchdowns in Sunday's 37-20 win, which included his 249th career TD pass. After the game, he spoke about his past comments about Romo.

"I was a big fan of Romo," he said, per The Athletic's Jon Machota . "I was. I was a fan of the Cowboys, and so it led into being a fan of the quarterback of the Cowboys. Frustrated at times, as he was, or as some fans are of me, and there was a tweet out there, right, that when I got drafted, that was brought back up. I was just a dumb fan at that time, too. I didn't know exactly what he was dealing with, you know what I mean?"

Prescott completed 26 of his 31 passes for 279 yards in the victory. It was a strong bounce-back performance after Dallas' season-opening loss to the New York Giants.

"He was awesome today and he's been awesome for a long time," former Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett said on NBC's Football Night in America on Sunday. "Eleven years as a starter. We had him as a rookie and he won 13 games. So, I wish people would just pull back and just appreciate that guy's greatness."

Prescott and the Cowboys (1-1) will return to action in Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens (1-1).
